stories.headline: Vatican City: Pope Leo mourns Spain’s train crash dead
stories.body: The Pope sent a telegram, signed by Cardinal Parolin, to Archbishop Francisco Cerro Chaves of Toledo, expressing his “deep sorrow” after two high-speed trains collided near Urda on Wednesday morning. He prayed for the eternal repose of the dead, comfort for families and a speedy recovery for the injured, encouraged rescue teams to persevere, and imparted his Apostolic Blessing.

stories.headline: Vatican City: Costa Rica’s president and Archbishop Gomez in the Apostolic Palace
stories.body: This morning the Pope received Costa Rica’s President Laura Fernández Delgado; talks with Cardinal Parolin and Archbishop Paul Gallagher covered security and migration in the region. Also received: Cardinal Víctor Manuel Fernández of the Doctrine of the Faith, Archbishop José Gomez of Los Angeles, Archbishop Mieczysław Mokrzycki of Lviv in Ukraine, and the Papal Foundation led by Ward Fitzgerald.

stories.headline: Vatican City: The Pope’s almoner is in Ukraine, Dnipro on his route
stories.body: Archbishop Luis Marín de San Martín, prefect of the Dicastery for the Service of Charity, is on a Oct. 27 to 30 mission to bring Pope Leo’s closeness to Ukrainians, visiting communities in Kyiv, Zaporizhzhia, Dnipro and Fastiv with both the Greek Catholic and Latin-rite Churches. The trip follows the Pope’s calls to Putin and Zelenskyy about besieged, starving Oleshky. At the Vatican, a winter collection of clothing, blankets, sleeping bags and canned food runs until Saturday.

stories.headline: Africa: Russia–Africa summit ends with 60-plus agreements
stories.body: At the Grand Kremlin Palace, Putin and the African Union chair, Burundi’s President Évariste Ndayishimiye, led a plenary with nearly 50 African countries under the motto “For Peace, Security and Development.” Putin said trade passed 27 billion dollars last year, up 50 percent since the last summit, and offered grain, fertilizer and training. The summit adopted a 2027 to 2029 action plan and an AI cooperation declaration, and organizers report more than 60 signed agreements. Eritrea’s Isaias Afwerki sees Putin on Friday.

stories.headline: Africa: Ebola passes 10,000 cases as the U.S. travel rule nears
stories.body: Congo’s Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak has topped 10,000 confirmed cases and is near 5,000 deaths across eight provinces, with Ituri and North Kivu worst hit. The WHO urges sustained testing, tracing and community outreach, since most new cases fall outside known chains of transmission. The CDC’s bar on U.S.-bound travelers who were in Congo within 21 days starts Tuesday, Nov. 3.

stories.headline: Africa: UN investigators warn drone war is spreading in Sudan
stories.body: The head of the UN fact-finding mission, Mohamed Chande Othman, told the General Assembly that October saw some of the deadliest single attacks of the war, including a drone strike in Blue Nile that killed at least 30 displaced people. He warned of repeated drone attacks on El Obeid in North Kordofan and found reasonable grounds that foreign weapons and personnel are fueling both sides.

stories.headline: Asia: Israel’s count is complete: Netanyahu bloc 53, opposition 48
stories.body: Israel’s Central Elections Committee finished counting Thursday, soldiers’ and diplomats’ ballots included. Likud leads with 27 seats, then Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar with 21; Netanyahu’s bloc holds 53, the opposition bloc 48 and Arab-led lists 19, so no one has the 61 needed. Official results come next Wednesday after integrity checks. Eisenkot met Yair Golan and Yair Lapid to coordinate, while Netanyahu’s camp alleged foreign interference and urged no deals with Arab parties, a charge Arab leaders called incitement.

stories.headline: Asia: Iran reports tankers hit mines in Hormuz as peace ideas circulate
stories.body: Iran says three tankers struck mines and caught fire while using an unauthorized southern route through the Strait of Hormuz, with a fourth hit east of the strait. Qatar’s seven-day plan is still on Tehran’s desk, with a reply expected by Saturday, though a senior Iranian official called it only “unacceptable ideas.” President Trump says Vice President Vance’s letter to security chief Mohsen Rezaei is about medical aid, not new talks, and keeps post-election strikes on the table.

stories.headline: Asia: North Korea fires about 10 short-range ballistic missiles
stories.body: Around 12:30 p.m. local time, North Korea launched about 10 short-range ballistic missiles from the Wonsan area into the sea off its east coast, flying roughly 250 kilometers, South Korea’s military said, its third round this month. Japan said they fell outside its economic zone and lodged a protest; Seoul, Washington and Tokyo stepped up monitoring.

stories.headline: Europe: Spain’s investigators: trains hit at 160 to 200 km/h
stories.body: Spain’s rail accident investigators said Thursday the Renfe train struck the stopped Iryo train at 8:53 Wednesday at an estimated 160 to 200 km/h. Their first note traces a signaling failure at 8:31 that forced manual, phoned instructions between the control center and drivers, a “chain of failures, instructions and actions” that ended in the collision without the safety barriers working. All hypotheses stay open; recorders are recovered, but drivers and controllers are not yet fit to be interviewed. The toll stands at 69 dead and more than 200 hurt, and Spain is in three days of mourning.

stories.headline: Europe: Dnipro station strike toll rises to 14
stories.body: Officials say 14 people died when a Russian jet-powered drone hit a platform at Dnipro’s main station as a train prepared to leave for Zaporizhzhia; 14 more were hurt, among them an 11-year-old boy, and six are critical. The Kremlin says three-way talks in Abu Dhabi could come only “after Nov. 4,” depending on the battlefield.

stories.headline: Europe: Christine Lagarde will leave the ECB on Feb. 7
stories.body: The European Central Bank president told her Governing Council this morning she will step down on Feb. 7, 2027, months before her term ends, and got a long standing ovation. EU leaders will now pick a successor, just as the bank prepares its digital euro pilot.

stories.headline: North America: Trump in Ohio, Obama on the trail, five days out
stories.body: In Chillicothe, Ohio, Wednesday night, the President campaigned for Vivek Ramaswamy for governor and Senator Jon Husted, promised a 5,000 dollar payment to every adult if Republicans hold both chambers, and floated Ohio for a new U.S. Space Academy. Former President Obama and Vice President Vance were also out making closing pitches. Election Day is Tuesday.

stories.headline: North America: Hegseth fires the Pentagon’s top military planner
stories.body: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth fired Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia, the Pentagon’s top military planner, after officials accused him of sharing information on the Iran and Ukraine wars with journalists. The case has been referred to the Justice Department.

stories.headline: North America: Mexico’s Senate lets 28 Navy SEALs train its marines
stories.body: Mexico’s Senate approved, by a wide margin, the entry of 28 U.S. Navy SEAL instructors to train Mexican Navy personnel in land and sea operations from today through April 15, at sites in Baja California Sur and the State of Mexico.

stories.headline: South America: Lula’s win reshapes Trump’s “orange wave”
stories.body: The Guardian’s analysis: Brazil, by 4.3 million votes, broke a string of pro-Trump wins from Argentina to Peru. Flávio Bolsonaro, now in Miami, briefly called himself the “true president-elect,” then backed off. Lula’s adviser Celso Amorim says Brazil will skip the U.S.-led Shield of the Americas coalition but seek “balanced” ties, and Trump says, “I like Lula.”

stories.headline: South America: Argentina’s YPF posts record output; Senate takes up mental health
stories.body: Argentina’s state oil company YPF reported record production and plans for billions in new investment, while the Senate resumed sessions to debate a new mental health law.

stories.headline: South America: Machado home in Venezuela; Rubio presses for fast reforms
stories.body: Opposition leader María Corina Machado is back in Venezuela after nearly a year away. Secretary of State Rubio said the interim authorities told Washington weeks ago she could return without interference, and that they have met every agreed deadline so far to replace the Supreme Court and electoral council before a presidential vote, which has no date yet.

stories.headline: Oceania: 250 million dollar climate grant for 14 Pacific nations
stories.body: The Green Climate Fund approved 250 million dollars, alongside about 809 million from the Asian Development Bank, for a decade of coastal, water, energy and health projects reaching 3.7 million Pacific islanders. Fiji also won 35.2 million dollars to protect its Great Sea Reef and restore 3,000 hectares of mangroves.

stories.headline: Oceania: Solomon Islands Prime Minister flown to Australia for care
stories.body: Prime Minister Matthew Wale was flown from Honiara to Australia for urgent medical treatment after being admitted to the National Referral Hospital. His condition has not been disclosed; former Prime Minister Manasseh Sogavare wished him a speedy recovery.

stories.headline: Oceania: Fiji hosts survivors of Pacific nuclear tests
stories.body: In Suva, a three-day dialogue through Friday gathers officials and survivors of more than 300 U.S., British and French nuclear tests to press for victim care and cleanup. Fiji’s defense minister urged testing nations to help fund veterans’ care; the findings go to the first review of the nuclear ban treaty in New York.

beats.title: MAGA / MAHA promises kept
beats.headline: Iran plan delivered; robot import order; peptide access opens.

stories.headline: Peace through strength: Qatar’s plan is on Iran’s desk
stories.body: Promise: end Iran’s nuclear threat without endless war. Action: with U.S. coordination, Qatar delivered a seven-day, step-by-step plan with outside guarantors, while the President keeps the threat of renewed strikes alive. Impact so far: Tehran publicly rejects it, but a formal reply is due this week; oil above 115 dollars shows what is at stake for families at the pump.

stories.headline: Made in America: a Section 232 order on robots and machine tools
stories.body: Promise: rebuild American manufacturing. Action: a Wednesday proclamation finds that imported robotics and industrial machinery threaten national security and orders Commerce and the Trade Representative to negotiate deals within 180 days, with tariffs, quotas or investment incentives possible later. Impact: no new tariffs yet; it is leverage for talks, and a signal to factories planning U.S. investment.

stories.headline: MAHA: Kennedy opens a path for six compounded peptides
stories.body: Promise: end what Secretary Kennedy calls the war on alternative medicine. Action: an interim HHS policy would let licensed compounding pharmacies prepare BPC-157, TB-500, epitalon, KPV, MOTS-c and semax with a prescription, tested ingredients and adverse-event reporting, after a two-week comment period. Impact: supporters gain safer, regulated access; FDA staff had advised against it, and doctors warn human trials are lacking.

stories.headline: Ending the Ukraine war: talks penciled in for after Nov. 4
stories.body: Promise: end the war. Action: the U.S. push has the Kremlin talking about three-way talks in Abu Dhabi “after Nov. 4,” the first in eight months, and the Oleshky truce has held. Impact: today’s strike on Dnipro’s station is a hard reminder that no wider ceasefire exists yet.

beats.headline: Tesla $403.30; merger needs 1.98 billion votes; Neuralink speech.

stories.headline: Neuralink: an ALS patient “speaks” 75 words a minute in week one
stories.body: Neuralink says a participant with ALS in its VOICE speech study reached 75 words per minute with a 5.8 percent word error rate on a 125,000-word vocabulary in the first week, near conversational pace. The figures are the company’s own and the study remains investigational, but it is a big step for people who have lost their voices.

stories.headline: Musk: SpaceX could build a U.S. phone carrier in “2 or 3 years”
stories.body: Musk answered Verizon’s CEO, who said a rival network would take four to six years and up to 500 billion dollars. SpaceX is in talks to lease space on about 80,000 cell sites and agreed this month to buy 800 MHz spectrum for a reported 8 billion dollars, pending FCC approval.

stories.headline: Tesla closed Thursday at $403.30 as merger math sinks in
stories.body: Tesla slipped 0.2 percent to 403.30 dollars Thursday on light volume, after Wednesday’s 404.22, and eased further after hours. Musk calls a Tesla–SpaceX combination “a good idea” but says it would need about 1.98 billion yes votes, a majority of all shares, which he called “quite a high hurdle”; independent committees have agreed no terms.

stories.headline: Musk: saving for retirement may be “pointless” in an age of abundance
stories.body: Musk argued again that superintelligent AI will make money matter far less, so long-term saving is less important, a view that Business Insider notes most financial planners would not follow.

beats.title: Space
beats.headline: Starship stages fired; China’s Qianfan grows; Starlink tonight.

stories.headline: Starship: both stages fired up; Flight 15 eyes double catches
stories.body: SpaceX finished Ship 42’s static fires, a full six-engine burn and a single-engine deorbit test, after Booster 22’s 33-engine firing. Flight 15 is targeted for November, aiming to catch both the booster and, for the first time, the ship in the tower’s chopsticks, if regulators agree.

stories.headline: China adds more Qianfan internet satellites from land and sea
stories.body: China launched more Qianfan constellation satellites on the sea-launched Gravity-1 and the land-based Zhuque-2E, building its second broadband network after Guowang.

stories.headline: Next up: Starlink 15-18 from California late tonight or Friday
stories.body: A Falcon 9 with 27 Starlink satellites, on booster B1093, has a window opening at 9:02 p.m. Pacific tonight, just after midnight Eastern, from Vandenberg, with a backup target Friday evening.

beats.title: NASA
beats.headline: Flawless spacewalk unrolls the seventh new solar array.

stories.headline: Spacewalk done: the seventh new solar array is unrolled
stories.body: Anil Menon and Canada’s Joshua Kutryk finished a 7-hour, 11-minute spacewalk at 3:08 p.m. Eastern, installing and unrolling the station’s seventh roll-out solar array on the port truss; Mission Control called it “essentially flawless.” They hooked up cables in orbital darkness, finished early and did prep work for the final array on Nov. 5. It was the 100th U.S. spacewalk from the station, and Kutryk became the first Canadian to walk in space since 2019. The eight arrays lift station power from about 160 to 215 kilowatts through its 2030 retirement.

stories.headline: Artemis III: the core stage now stands between its boosters
stories.body: NASA posted images of the SLS core stage joined to its twin solid rocket boosters in Kennedy’s Vehicle Assembly Building. After checkout, the rocket rolls to Pad 39B for fueling and countdown practice ahead of a 2027 Earth-orbit test of lunar lander operations.

stories.headline: Reid Wiseman, Artemis II commander, named JPL deputy director
stories.body: Caltech named Reid Wiseman, who commanded the Artemis II flight around the Moon, deputy director of NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory. NASA is also hosting media this week at a lunar-landing simulator at Ames.

beats.headline: Miami mourns Father Nguyen; Pope receives Gomez, Costa Rica.

stories.headline: Miami: Father Joseph Long Nguyen, first pastor of Our Lady of La Vang, dies at 62
stories.body: Father Nguyen was found dead Tuesday in the rectory of Our Lady of La Vang Parish in Hallandale Beach. Born in Vietnam in 1964, he reached the priesthood through Canada and the U.S., was ordained in 2002, and led the Vietnamese community from mission to full parish in July 2023, calling it “our second home.” Funeral arrangements are pending. Eternal rest grant unto him, O Lord.

stories.headline: Miami: This weekend around the archdiocese
stories.body: Friday at 8 p.m., the Rosary of Men prays for world peace in Spanish, Portuguese and English at Corpus Christi, 3220 NW Seventh Ave. Saturday brings an Oktoberfest dinner at 5 at St. Gabriel in Pompano Beach and a family night from 7 at St. Martin de Porres in Leisure City. Sunday is All Saints; Monday, All Souls.

stories.headline: Miami: Little Flower’s new organ marks a parish century
stories.body: Coral Gables’ Church of the Little Flower celebrated 100 years with a centennial Mass and a new 3,035-pipe C. B. Fisk Opus 166 organ, blessed by Archbishop Wenski: “Let your music lift our hearts beyond ourselves.”

stories.headline: Spain: a parish priest at the crash site
stories.body: In Urda, Father José Miguel Fernández is with relatives at the school turned information center, saying families heal better when they can say goodbye. The Pope’s telegram went to Toledo’s Archbishop Cerro Chaves.

stories.headline: U.S.: Archbishop Gomez with the Pope; the Papal Foundation too
stories.body: Los Angeles’ Archbishop José Gomez and the Papal Foundation, which funds Church projects in poorer countries, were both received this morning.

stories.headline: Ukraine: the Pope’s charity chief brings winter aid toward Dnipro
stories.body: On the day Lviv’s Archbishop Mieczysław Mokrzycki saw the Pope, Archbishop Luis Marín de San Martín, the Spanish Augustinian who now leads the Pope’s charity office, was in Ukraine on a mission through Kyiv, Zaporizhzhia, Dnipro and Fastiv, alongside Greek and Latin Catholics. A Vatican winter collection for Ukrainians runs through Saturday.

stories.headline: Appointments and installations: Lucera-Troia today; Metuchen, Joliet
stories.body: Today Bishop Giorgio Ferretti takes possession of Lucera-Troia in Italy; Saturday Georgios Altouvas is installed at Syros in Greece and Michele Di Tolve at Chioggia. Bishop Michael Saporito was installed as Metuchen’s sixth bishop, and Bishop Brendan Cahill comes to Joliet on Nov. 11. No new Vatican appointments were published today.

beats.title: Signs of the times
beats.headline: Countdown still Oct. 27; Medjugorje Oct. 25; 596 in Mobile.

stories.headline: Countdown to the Kingdom: checked this evening, latest post is still Oct. 27
stories.body: Checked again this evening, the newest post remains Tuesday’s “How to Offer Your Ordinary Acts in the Divine Will,” drawing on Servant of God Luisa Piccarreta. Before it: Marija’s Oct. 25 Medjugorje message, two Oct. 23 essays, and the Oct. 20 and 21 messages attributed to Pedro Regis. The site reminds readers that the Church alone judges authenticity.

stories.headline: Medjugorje, Oct. 25 (latest): “Be my extended hands of love and peace”
stories.body: The latest monthly message through Marija, Oct. 25, 2026: “A fire of hatred and wars is spreading in the hearts of people who do not want peace but their own weak interests. That is why, little children, you be prayer and my extended hands of love and peace for all those who are far from my motherly heart. Pray more strongly and more for the peace that God desires to give you.” The next is due Nov. 25.

stories.headline: Reading the night beside the message
stories.body: Overnight brought both the fire and the hands: missiles over the sea off Korea, a drone on a Ukrainian train platform, and a grieving Spain; and also a peace plan on Iran’s desk, talk of Abu Dhabi, and a priest in Urda walking with families. The message asks for prayer and for us to be the extended hands.

stories.headline: Revival: 596 decisions for Christ in Mobile
stories.body: UniteUS’s Tuesday night at the University of South Alabama drew about 3,500 people; 596 made decisions to follow Christ, and 52 were baptized right after, some in truck-bed baptismals outside.

stories.headline: Mind and machine: Neuralink’s speech implant
stories.body: As brain implants move from typing to speech, a reminder from the Church’s teaching on technology: such tools are a gift when they restore what illness took and serve the person, never when they treat the person as a product.

stories.headline: Digital money, soberly: the ECB loses its digital euro champion
stories.body: Christine Lagarde, the strongest voice for the digital euro, leaves in February. The legislation is still under negotiation, with the next round Nov. 5, and the pilot is planned for late 2027 at the earliest; issuance could come in 2029 only if lawmakers act.

stories.headline: Tonight: VOUS Worship’s “Man Alive,” free at Bayfront Park
stories.body: Doors open at 6 at the FPL Solar Amphitheater, music runs 7 to 10, and admission is free. Earlier, from 4 to 8, Hialeah Cares hosts a free Halloween party at Miami Dade College Hialeah.

stories.headline: Opening today at PAMM: Picasso, Klee, Matisse
stories.body: Nearly 100 modern masterworks from Berlin’s Museum Berggruen, including Matisse cut-outs, Giacometti sculptures and early Cubist Picassos, go on view at the Pérez Art Museum today through Feb. 28.

stories.headline: This weekend: Flugtag, Viernes Culturales, jazz at MOCA
stories.body: Friday brings Viernes Culturales on Calle Ocho and free jazz with pianist Mike Gerber at MOCA North Miami at 8. Saturday at 10, Red Bull Flugtag sends 30 homemade flying machines, including a Cuban sandwich, off a ramp into Biscayne Bay at Bayfront Park; it is free with RSVP. stories.body: Giannis Antetokounmpo had 24 points and 18 rebounds in his first win as a Heat player, and Bam Adebayo added 24 points and nine rebounds, passing Udonis Haslem as Miami’s career rebounding leader. Miami led from a 34–25 first quarter to end an 0–4 start. Next: Indiana at Kaseya Center, Friday at 8.

stories.headline: Star Wars: Lucasfilm Games plans more small surprises
stories.body: After Galactic Racer and Zero Company, Lucasfilm Games says it will keep making smaller Star Wars games alongside the big ones.

stories.headline: Star Wars: Starfighter’s scale, and Ahsoka in January
stories.body: Shawn Levy’s Starfighter, with Ryan Gosling, opens May 28, 2027, and is reportedly budgeted above The Force Awakens; Eva Mendes is rumored to join him. Ahsoka Season 2 arrives Jan. 20 on Disney+.

stories.headline: North America: Mexico’s Senate lets 28 Navy SEALs train its marines
stories.body: Mexico’s Senate approved, by a wide margin, the entry of 28 U.S. Navy SEAL instructors to train Mexican Navy personnel in land and sea operations from today through April 15, at sites in Baja California Sur and the State of Mexico.

stories.headline: North America: A quiet Atlantic for the last days of October
stories.body: The National Hurricane Center shows no tropical cyclones in the Atlantic, Caribbean or Gulf, and none expected to form in the next seven days, welcome news for South Florida with a month of hurricane season left.

stories.headline: South America: Lula’s win reshapes Trump’s “orange wave”
stories.body: The Guardian’s analysis: Brazil, by 4.3 million votes, broke a string of pro-Trump wins from Argentina to Peru. Flávio Bolsonaro, now in Miami, briefly called himself the “true president-elect,” then backed off. Lula’s adviser Celso Amorim says Brazil will skip the U.S.-led Shield of the Americas coalition but seek “balanced” ties, and Trump says, “I like Lula.”

stories.headline: South America: Argentina’s YPF posts record output; Senate takes up mental health
stories.body: Argentina’s state oil company YPF reported record production and plans for billions in new investment, while the Senate resumed sessions to debate a new mental health law.

stories.headline: South America: Machado home in Venezuela; Rubio presses for fast reforms
stories.body: Opposition leader María Corina Machado is back in Venezuela after nearly a year away. Secretary of State Rubio said the interim authorities told Washington weeks ago she could return without interference, and that they have met every agreed deadline so far to replace the Supreme Court and electoral council before a presidential vote, which has no date yet.

stories.headline: Oceania: 250 million dollar climate grant for 14 Pacific nations
stories.body: The Green Climate Fund approved 250 million dollars, alongside about 809 million from the Asian Development Bank, for a decade of coastal, water, energy and health projects reaching 3.7 million Pacific islanders. Fiji also won 35.2 million dollars to protect its Great Sea Reef and restore 3,000 hectares of mangroves.

stories.headline: Oceania: Solomon Islands Prime Minister flown to Australia for care
stories.body: Prime Minister Matthew Wale was flown from Honiara to Australia for urgent medical treatment after being admitted to the National Referral Hospital. His condition has not been disclosed; former Prime Minister Manasseh Sogavare wished him a speedy recovery.

stories.headline: Oceania: Fiji hosts survivors of Pacific nuclear tests
stories.body: In Suva, a three-day dialogue through Friday gathers officials and survivors of more than 300 U.S., British and French nuclear tests to press for victim care and cleanup. Fiji’s defense minister urged testing nations to help fund veterans’ care; the findings go to the first review of the nuclear ban treaty in New York.

image.alt: Vatican City: Pope Leo mourns Spain’s train crash dead

beats.title: MAGA / MAHA promises kept
beats.headline: Iran plan delivered; robot import order; peptide access opens.

stories.headline: Peace through strength: Qatar’s plan is on Iran’s desk
stories.body: Promise: end Iran’s nuclear threat without endless war. Action: with U.S. coordination, Qatar delivered a seven-day, step-by-step plan with outside guarantors, while the President keeps the threat of renewed strikes alive. Impact so far: Tehran publicly rejects it, but a formal reply is due this week; oil above 115 dollars shows what is at stake for families at the pump.

stories.headline: Made in America: a Section 232 order on robots and machine tools
stories.body: Promise: rebuild American manufacturing. Action: a Wednesday proclamation finds that imported robotics and industrial machinery threaten national security and orders Commerce and the Trade Representative to negotiate deals within 180 days, with tariffs, quotas or investment incentives possible later. Impact: no new tariffs yet; it is leverage for talks, and a signal to factories planning U.S. investment.

stories.headline: MAHA: Kennedy opens a path for six compounded peptides
stories.body: Promise: end what Secretary Kennedy calls the war on alternative medicine. Action: an interim HHS policy would let licensed compounding pharmacies prepare BPC-157, TB-500, epitalon, KPV, MOTS-c and semax with a prescription, tested ingredients and adverse-event reporting, after a two-week comment period. Impact: supporters gain safer, regulated access; FDA staff had advised against it, and doctors warn human trials are lacking.

stories.headline: Ending the Ukraine war: talks penciled in for after Nov. 4
stories.body: Promise: end the war. Action: the U.S. push has the Kremlin talking about three-way talks in Abu Dhabi “after Nov. 4,” the first in eight months, and the Oleshky truce has held. Impact: today’s strike on Dnipro’s station is a hard reminder that no wider ceasefire exists yet.

image.alt: Peace through strength: Qatar’s plan is on Iran’s desk

beats.title: Musk world
beats.headline: Neuralink speech at 75 words a minute; SpaceX eyes phones.

stories.headline: Neuralink: an ALS patient “speaks” 75 words a minute in week one
stories.body: Neuralink says a participant with ALS in its VOICE speech study reached 75 words per minute with a 5.8 percent word error rate on a 125,000-word vocabulary in the first week, near conversational pace. The figures are the company’s own and the study remains investigational, but it is a big step for people who have lost their voices.

stories.headline: Musk: SpaceX could build a U.S. phone carrier in “2 or 3 years”
stories.body: Musk answered Verizon’s CEO, who said a rival network would take four to six years and up to 500 billion dollars. SpaceX is in talks to lease space on about 80,000 cell sites and agreed this month to buy 800 MHz spectrum for a reported 8 billion dollars, pending FCC approval.

stories.headline: Tesla closed Wednesday at $404.22 as merger talk simmers
stories.body: Tesla slipped 0.8 percent Wednesday after Tuesday’s 4 percent jump. Musk has said a Tesla–SpaceX combination would be a good idea but noted it would need a majority of all Tesla shares, and the independent committees have not agreed on terms.

stories.headline: Musk: saving for retirement may be “pointless” in an age of abundance
stories.body: Musk argued again that superintelligent AI will make money matter far less, so long-term saving is less important, a view that Business Insider notes most financial planners would not follow.

image.alt: Neuralink: an ALS patient “speaks” 75 words a minute in week one

beats.title: Space
beats.headline: Starship stages fired; China’s Qianfan grows; Starlink tonight.

stories.headline: Starship: both stages fired up; Flight 15 eyes double catches
stories.body: SpaceX finished Ship 42’s static fires, a full six-engine burn and a single-engine deorbit test, after Booster 22’s 33-engine firing. Flight 15 is targeted for November, aiming to catch both the booster and, for the first time, the ship in the tower’s chopsticks, if regulators agree.

stories.headline: China adds more Qianfan internet satellites from land and sea
stories.body: China launched more Qianfan constellation satellites on the sea-launched Gravity-1 and the land-based Zhuque-2E, building its second broadband network after Guowang.

stories.headline: Next up: Starlink 15-18 from California late tonight or Friday
stories.body: A Falcon 9 with 27 Starlink satellites, on booster B1093, has a window opening at 9:02 p.m. Pacific tonight, just after midnight Eastern, from Vandenberg, with a backup target Friday evening.

image.alt: Starship: both stages fired up; Flight 15 eyes double catches

beats.title: NASA
beats.headline: Spacewalk under way for a new solar array.

stories.headline: Spacewalk under way: Menon and Kutryk install a new solar array
stories.body: NASA’s Anil Menon and Canada’s Joshua Kutryk went out at 7:57 a.m. Eastern to install the station’s seventh roll-out solar array on the port truss, with Menon riding Canadarm2 to carry it. It is Menon’s fourth spacewalk, Kutryk’s first, the fifth ever by a Canadian, and U.S. spacewalk 100. The array will power the station through its eventual controlled deorbit; the eighth and final one goes up Nov. 5.

stories.headline: Artemis III: the core stage now stands between its boosters
stories.body: NASA posted images of the SLS core stage joined to its twin solid rocket boosters in Kennedy’s Vehicle Assembly Building. After checkout, the rocket rolls to Pad 39B for fueling and countdown practice ahead of a 2027 Earth-orbit test of lunar lander operations.

stories.headline: Reid Wiseman, Artemis II commander, named JPL deputy director
stories.body: Caltech named Reid Wiseman, who commanded the Artemis II flight around the Moon, deputy director of NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory. NASA is also hosting media this week at a lunar-landing simulator at Ames.

beats.title: Catholic
beats.headline: Miami mourns Father Nguyen; Pope receives Gomez, Costa Rica.

stories.headline: Miami: Father Joseph Long Nguyen, first pastor of Our Lady of La Vang, dies at 62
stories.body: Father Nguyen was found dead Tuesday in the rectory of Our Lady of La Vang Parish in Hallandale Beach. Born in Vietnam in 1964, he reached the priesthood through Canada and the U.S., was ordained in 2002, and led the Vietnamese community from mission to full parish in July 2023, calling it “our second home.” Funeral arrangements are pending. Eternal rest grant unto him, O Lord.

stories.headline: Miami: This weekend around the archdiocese
stories.body: Friday at 8 p.m., the Rosary of Men prays for world peace in Spanish, Portuguese and English at Corpus Christi, 3220 NW Seventh Ave. Saturday brings an Oktoberfest dinner at 5 at St. Gabriel in Pompano Beach and a family night from 7 at St. Martin de Porres in Leisure City. Sunday is All Saints; Monday, All Souls.

stories.headline: Miami: Little Flower’s new organ marks a parish century
stories.body: Coral Gables’ Church of the Little Flower celebrated 100 years with a centennial Mass and a new 3,035-pipe C. B. Fisk Opus 166 organ, blessed by Archbishop Wenski: “Let your music lift our hearts beyond ourselves.”

stories.headline: Spain: a parish priest at the crash site
stories.body: In Urda, Father José Miguel Fernández is with relatives at the school turned information center, saying families heal better when they can say goodbye. The Pope’s telegram went to Toledo’s Archbishop Cerro Chaves.

stories.headline: U.S.: Archbishop Gomez with the Pope; the Papal Foundation too
stories.body: Los Angeles’ Archbishop José Gomez and the Papal Foundation, which funds Church projects in poorer countries, were both received this morning.

stories.headline: Ukraine: Lviv’s Latin archbishop sees the Pope on a hard day
stories.body: Archbishop Mieczysław Mokrzycki of Lviv was received the same morning a drone killed at least 13 at Dnipro’s station.

stories.headline: Appointments and installations: Lucera-Troia today; Metuchen, Joliet
stories.body: Today Bishop Giorgio Ferretti takes possession of Lucera-Troia in Italy; Saturday Georgios Altouvas is installed at Syros in Greece and Michele Di Tolve at Chioggia. Bishop Michael Saporito was installed as Metuchen’s sixth bishop, and Bishop Brendan Cahill comes to Joliet on Nov. 11. No new Vatican appointments were published today.

beats.title: Signs of the times
beats.headline: Countdown still Oct. 27; Medjugorje Oct. 25; 596 in Mobile.

stories.headline: Countdown to the Kingdom: checked this morning, latest post is still Oct. 27
stories.body: The newest post remains Tuesday’s “How to Offer Your Ordinary Acts in the Divine Will,” drawing on Servant of God Luisa Piccarreta. Before it: Marija’s Oct. 25 Medjugorje message, two Oct. 23 essays, and the Oct. 20 and 21 messages attributed to Pedro Regis. The site reminds readers that the Church alone judges authenticity.

stories.headline: Medjugorje, Oct. 25 (latest): “Be my extended hands of love and peace”
stories.body: The latest monthly message through Marija, Oct. 25, 2026: “A fire of hatred and wars is spreading in the hearts of people who do not want peace but their own weak interests. That is why, little children, you be prayer and my extended hands of love and peace for all those who are far from my motherly heart. Pray more strongly and more for the peace that God desires to give you.” The next is due Nov. 25.

stories.headline: Reading the night beside the message
stories.body: Overnight brought both the fire and the hands: missiles over the sea off Korea, a drone on a Ukrainian train platform, and a grieving Spain; and also a peace plan on Iran’s desk, talk of Abu Dhabi, and a priest in Urda walking with families. The message asks for prayer and for us to be the extended hands.

stories.headline: Revival: 596 decisions for Christ in Mobile
stories.body: UniteUS’s Tuesday night at the University of South Alabama drew about 3,500 people; 596 made decisions to follow Christ, and 52 were baptized right after, some in truck-bed baptismals outside.

stories.headline: Mind and machine: Neuralink’s speech implant
stories.body: As brain implants move from typing to speech, a reminder from the Church’s teaching on technology: such tools are a gift when they restore what illness took and serve the person, never when they treat the person as a product.

stories.headline: Digital money, soberly: the ECB loses its digital euro champion
stories.body: Christine Lagarde, the strongest voice for the digital euro, leaves in February. The legislation is still under negotiation, with the next round Nov. 5, and the pilot is planned for late 2027 at the earliest; issuance could come in 2029 only if lawmakers act.

beats.headline: VOUS free tonight; PAMM opens Picasso; Flugtag Saturday.

stories.headline: Tonight: VOUS Worship’s “Man Alive,” free at Bayfront Park
stories.body: Doors open at 6 at the FPL Solar Amphitheater, music runs 7 to 10, and admission is free. Earlier, from 4 to 8, Hialeah Cares hosts a free Halloween party at Miami Dade College Hialeah.

stories.headline: Opening today at PAMM: Picasso, Klee, Matisse
stories.body: Nearly 100 modern masterworks from Berlin’s Museum Berggruen, including Matisse cut-outs, Giacometti sculptures and early Cubist Picassos, go on view at the Pérez Art Museum today through Feb. 28.

stories.headline: This weekend: Flugtag, Viernes Culturales, jazz at MOCA
stories.body: Friday brings Viernes Culturales on Calle Ocho and free jazz with pianist Mike Gerber at MOCA North Miami at 8. Saturday at 10, Red Bull Flugtag sends 30 homemade flying machines, including a Cuban sandwich, off a ramp into Biscayne Bay at Bayfront Park; it is free with RSVP. stories.headline: Heat win! Giannis and Bam lead a 129–117 win in Atlanta
stories.body: Giannis Antetokounmpo had 24 points and 18 rebounds in his first win as a Heat player, and Bam Adebayo added 24 points and nine rebounds, passing Udonis Haslem as Miami’s career rebounding leader. Miami led from a 34–25 first quarter to end an 0–4 start. Next: Indiana at Kaseya Center, Friday at 8.

stories.headline: Star Wars: Lucasfilm Games plans more small surprises
stories.body: After Galactic Racer and Zero Company, Lucasfilm Games says it will keep making smaller Star Wars games alongside the big ones.

stories.headline: Star Wars: Starfighter’s scale, and Ahsoka in January
stories.body: Shawn Levy’s Starfighter, with Ryan Gosling, opens May 28, 2027, and is reportedly budgeted above The Force Awakens; Eva Mendes is rumored to join him. Ahsoka Season 2 arrives Jan. 20 on Disney+.

beats.title: World
beats.headline: Pope greets migrant ministers; Israel 53–48; Putin meets Abiy.

stories.headline: Vatican City: Pope greets Chicago volunteers who visit detained migrants
stories.body: At the end of this morning’s audience, Pope Leo greeted about thirty members of Chicago’s Coalition for Spiritual and Public Leadership, priests, deacons, students and lay leaders who visit immigrants held at the Broadview ICE facility. Since May they have made more than 135 visits to 725 detainees. They brought him items from migrants telling their stories; Scalabrinian laywoman Abigail Ortiz Valles said every visit to Broadview is an encounter with Christ’s Passion. A pilgrimage group from St. Jude in New Lenox, Illinois, including the Pope’s brother John Joseph Prevost, was also in the square.

stories.headline: Vatican City: Pope Leo back in St. Peter’s Square for the audience
stories.body: Pope Leo rode the popemobile through St. Peter’s Square this morning, Rome time, and gave his Wednesday catechesis outdoors. Continuing his series on Gaudium et Spes, he said faith “enriches and brings to fulfillment every culture it encounters” and must itself “become a culture that is shaped by Christ.” Beforehand he met Mercedes-Benz executives marking a century of the Popemobile, urging that technology serve human dignity, creation and the common good.
stories.why: The catechesis series on the Council’s Gaudium et Spes continues weekly ahead of the Nov. 6 trip to South America.

stories.headline: Vatican City: Cardinal Romeo’s funeral this morning; the Pope’s November calendar
stories.body: The funeral of Cardinal Paolo Romeo, Palermo’s archbishop from 2006 to 2015, is at 11 a.m. Rome time, 6 a.m. Eastern, in Acireale’s cathedral. In his condolence telegram, Pope Leo called him a “dear brother who generously served the Gospel,” recalling his years as papal representative in Haiti, Colombia, Canada and Italy. The Vatican also released the Pope’s liturgies ahead: All Souls’ Mass at Rome’s Verano Cemetery on Nov. 2, a Mass for deceased cardinals and bishops on Nov. 5, then the Nov. 6–17 trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru.

stories.headline: Vatican City: Saint Peter’s Basilica turns 400 on Nov. 18
stories.body: On returning from South America, the Pope will celebrate Mass on Nov. 18 for the fourth centenary of the dedication of Saint Peter’s Basilica, consecrated in 1626. On Dec. 8 he goes to Piazza di Spagna for the traditional act of veneration of Mary Immaculate. The trip itself will include a meeting with survivors of clergy abuse, the Vatican confirmed Tuesday.

stories.headline: Africa: Putin meets Abiy; trade has more than doubled this year
stories.body: Putin received Ethiopia’s Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed at the Kremlin this evening, Moscow time, on the sidelines of the Russia–Africa summit. Putin said trade topped 1.3 billion dollars from January to September, more than double all of 2025, and pointed to energy, farming, industry, health and space; Abiy spoke of nuclear cooperation. No public word yet on Eritrea, whose President Isaias Afwerki sees Putin on Friday, among 11 meetings that day.
stories.why: Russia has offered to host Ethiopia–Eritrea contacts; Friday’s Isaias meeting is the one to watch.

stories.headline: Africa: U.S. will bar travelers who were in Congo within 21 days
stories.body: The CDC says that from Nov. 3 through Dec. 18, everyone boarding a flight to the United States must sign that they have not been in Congo in the previous 21 days, and U.S. citizens are included. The count is now 10,141 confirmed cases and 4,928 deaths, with 50 to 80 new cases a day across eight provinces. Genetic testing links the Kenyan and Nigerian cases to Congo’s outbreak; both patients passed through Entebbe airport on Oct. 3. Africa CDC’s Jean Kaseya warned Europe to prepare.

stories.headline: Africa: Nyala market strike in Darfur; tolls range from 36 to 188
stories.body: An army drone struck a crowded market in Nyala, South Darfur, on Monday night. Doctors Without Borders received 36 bodies and more than 150 wounded; the Emergency Lawyers group says more than 100 died, and the Tasees coalition puts it at 188. Witnesses told AP some of those killed were civilians selling food to fighters. The figures cannot be independently checked.

stories.headline: Africa: Abiy and Isaias both in Moscow as Russia offers to mediate
stories.body: The third Russia–Africa summit opens today in Moscow with 48 countries taking part, 22 led by heads of state. Ethiopia’s Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed meets Putin today; Eritrea’s President Isaias Afwerki, who arrived Tuesday, sees him Friday. Russia has offered a venue for Ethiopia–Eritrea contacts, and China says a special envoy will tour the region, but neither neighbor has accepted. On the ground, federal forces captured senior Tigrayan commander Maj. Gen. Yohannes Woldegiyorgis on Oct. 26, while Fano militias in Amhara attack the supply roads into Tigray.
stories.why: Both leaders in one city is the closest the two sides have come to talks since ties broke down; Ethiopia says it will talk only on three conditions.

stories.headline: Africa: Ebola outbreak is now the world’s second largest ever recorded
stories.body: With 10,060 confirmed cases and 4,887 deaths, Congo’s Bundibugyo outbreak is now the second-largest Ebola epidemic on record, and more than 2,700 of the infected are children, Save the Children says. A nurse was killed in an attack on health workers answering an alert. Kenya has nine linked cases, and Nigeria’s single case has been evacuated to Switzerland. The Norwegian Refugee Council is calling for an urgent scale-up of the response, and a treatment trial called TUMAINI began in Bunia on Oct. 23.

stories.headline: Africa: UN warns sieges in Kordofan and Blue Nile could repeat El Fasher
stories.body: Marking a year since El Fasher fell to the Rapid Support Forces, UN officials called for accountability and an immediate ceasefire and urged both the army and the RSF to pull their forces out of cities. The UN’s genocide-prevention adviser warned that sieges in Kordofan and Blue Nile could open the way to new atrocities. Amnesty says fewer than 70,000 people remain in a city that once held more than a million, and 17 of the 19 people it interviewed had been detained.

stories.headline: Asia: Netanyahu’s bloc slips to 53 as Israel’s count nears its end
stories.body: With about 93 percent of ordinary ballots counted, Israel’s Central Elections Committee has Netanyahu’s bloc at 53 seats, Eisenkot’s bloc at 48 and Arab-led parties at a record 19; 61 is a majority. Likud has slipped to 26 seats, with Eisenkot’s Yashar at 21. Somewhere between 430,000 and 600,000 double-envelope ballots, mostly soldiers and officials, are still to be counted over the next couple of days and could move seats. Democrats leader Yair Golan says formal coalition talks with Eisenkot and Yair Lapid begin Thursday.
stories.why: Eisenkot now faces a hard choice: an unprecedented pact with Arab parties, or a unity deal or new elections that keep Netanyahu in play.

stories.headline: Asia: Qatar presses Iran on inspectors as Trump says “finish the job”
stories.body: Axios reports Qatar, backed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Egypt and Turkey, is urging Iran to let UN inspectors back into its bombed nuclear sites in return for oil waivers and some unfrozen funds for food. Iran says it will seek Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei’s approval within days. Trump told Axios talks are happening through mediators but “we need to finish the job, either through a deal or another way.” U.S. and Israeli officials describe a possible week of heavy strikes after the midterms if there is no deal.

stories.headline: Asia: Overnight count puts Netanyahu’s bloc at 54, short of a majority
stories.body: With about 71 percent of votes counted by Wednesday morning in Israel, Netanyahu’s bloc has 54 of 120 seats, the Eisenkot-led opposition 47, and Arab-led parties 19. Likud leads with 27 seats, ahead of Eisenkot’s Yashar at about 21, and turnout was 77.7 percent. Eisenkot has left the door open to working with Arab parties under conditions. Soldiers’ ballots are still being counted. President Trump said Netanyahu “did very well” and the race “might be winning or tie.”

stories.headline: Asia: Gulf states draft a peace deal as Houthis claim a refinery strike
stories.body: The Guardian reports Gulf states are building a multipart deal: Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz within four days of sanctions being lifted, and the Houthis would withdraw. The U.S. and Europe also want UN inspectors readmitted to Iran. Iran had earlier demanded seven days. Meanwhile the Houthis say they hit Saudi Arabia’s Ras Tanura refinery, causing a fire, with a ballistic missile, which Riyadh has not confirmed, and the Wall Street Journal reports the U.S. told Gulf allies to prepare for a “short, intense” campaign against Iran after the midterms.

stories.headline: Asia: Cyclone Arnab kills three in Andhra Pradesh after overnight landfall
stories.body: Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coast between 2 and 8 a.m. local time Wednesday and weakened to a severe cyclonic storm. Three people died, one under a falling tree in Bhimavaram and two from downed live wires. About 57,000 people are in relief camps in Andhra Pradesh and 30,000 were evacuated in Odisha, with crops on roughly 70,900 hectares damaged.

stories.headline: Europe: Zelenskyy wins Dutch and British aid; Abu Dhabi talks by Nov. 10
stories.body: In the Netherlands, Zelenskyy secured a 500 million euro military package, and Britain announced what it calls its biggest-ever support package, about 13 billion dollars for 2027. He expects three-way peace talks in Abu Dhabi by Nov. 10, though no date is set. An adviser to Melania Trump says Putin asked for her as mediator and that Russia proposed widening the Oleshky truce across more of Kherson, which Ukraine accepted.

stories.headline: Europe: Overnight, a missile and 88 drones; fire in Kharkiv injures a child
stories.body: Russia fired an Iskander ballistic missile and 88 attack drones, 38 of them jet-powered, overnight, Ukraine’s Air Force said; 71 drones were downed and eight sites were hit. A large fire broke out in Kharkiv’s Osnovianskyi district, injuring five people, among them a four-year-old. Across Ukraine, Russian attacks killed two people and injured 17 over the past day.

stories.headline: Europe: Oleshky truce passes 30 hours “without a single incident”
stories.body: Ukraine’s human rights commissioner Dmytro Lubinets says the first 30 hours of the Oleshky ceasefire passed with no incidents. Russia’s rights commissioner Tatyana Lantratova says it runs until 10:59 p.m. Moscow time on Nov. 1. Oleshky, across the Dnipro from Kherson, is under Russian occupation; the truce is meant to let civilians leave and supplies get in once roads are de-mined.

stories.headline: Europe: Trump hopes to meet Putin and Zelenskyy; France braces for protests
stories.body: Back from Texas overnight, President Trump said he hopes to meet Putin and Zelenskyy soon and that “a lot of progress” has been made; Putin has said Russia is ready to resume U.S.-mediated talks next month. In France, a Ligue 1 match in Lyon was moved because of nationwide protests planned for Saturday over living costs and school conditions. Turkey says it will load fuel at its first nuclear plant, Akkuyu, within weeks.

stories.headline: North America: Trump ends Biden’s methane rule at a Lubbock rally
stories.body: At Tuesday night’s rally in Lubbock, Texas, the President announced he is ending the Biden-era methane rule for oil and gas, claiming 45 billion dollars in savings and 210 million more barrels of oil. The rule had been projected to prevent 58 million tons of methane emissions by 2038. Environmental Defense Fund’s Fred Krupp called the repeal a “free pass” for polluters. Supporters say it will lower energy costs as fuel prices stay high during the Iran war.

stories.headline: North America: On the tarmac, Trump welcomes Flávio Bolsonaro and eyes Xi talks
stories.body: Returning to Joint Base Andrews overnight, the President said he would “approve” of Brazil’s defeated candidate Flávio Bolsonaro coming to the U.S., calling Brazil’s election “very strange.” He said a nuclear-disarmament meeting with China’s Xi Jinping is scheduled and that he will attend the ASEAN summit in Manila in November. The midterm elections are Tuesday, Nov. 3.

stories.headline: North America: WSJ: Gulf allies told to expect strikes on Iran after the vote
stories.body: The Wall Street Journal reports the U.S. has told several Gulf countries to prepare for a “short, intense military campaign” against Iran after the Nov. 3 midterms. A Patriot battery is moving from Texas to the region, troops have been pulled from exposed bases, and bombers are being readied.

stories.headline: South America: Trump welcomes Flávio Bolsonaro, calling the family “fine people”
stories.body: Trump said Wednesday he approved Flávio Bolsonaro’s arrival in the U.S. after his defeat in Brazil’s presidential election. The family left Brazil through Argentina and Ecuador, and the U.S. granted them visas, though Bolsonaro refused to hand over his passports in a Brazilian money-laundering investigation.

stories.headline: South America: Flávio Bolsonaro lands in Miami despite a court travel ban
stories.body: Brazil’s defeated presidential candidate arrived in Miami on Tuesday, met by his brother Eduardo, O Globo reports, despite a judicial ban on travel. President Trump said overnight he would approve of the visit. Brazil’s Federal Police have canceled his passports.

stories.headline: South America: Delcy Rodríguez retraces Machado’s route: “Let no one interfere”
stories.body: Venezuela’s acting president toured Aragua and other states along the road María Corina Machado traveled on her return, warning “radical sectors” not to meddle with the country’s “stability.” She promised relief “soon” from worsening blackouts, citing 7,400 megawatts to be added with General Electric and Argentina’s Impsa. She called Machado’s trip a “show.”

stories.headline: South America: U.S. soldiers train in Colombia through Nov. 11
stories.body: More than 300 U.S. troops are at Tolemaida, Colombia’s largest base, for the Vanguardia del Sur exercise on counternarcotics, illegal mining, drones and medical evacuation. Critics in Congress say lawmakers must authorize it; the government says training missions don’t need approval.

stories.headline: Oceania: Australia’s inflation jumps to 4.3 percent, driven by fuel
stories.body: Headline inflation rose to 4.3 percent in September, and Treasurer Jim Chalmers blamed the Middle East war and fuel prices. The Reserve Bank’s chief economist says he sees no recession ahead. The Star casino group was also fined 260 million dollars.

stories.headline: Oceania: Bomb threat at Parliament House as MPs’ safety stays in focus
stories.body: Federal police searched the Senate wing after a bomb threat shortly before lunch and found nothing. Police told a hearing there were nearly 800 threats against MPs in six months, and Senator Fatima Payman apologized to Helen Haines for remarks about the attack that cost the MP both legs.

stories.headline: Oceania: Marles meets Hegseth; Rocket Lab flies from New Zealand
stories.body: Defence Minister Richard Marles met U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth at the ASEAN defence ministers’ meeting on the sidelines of the regional talks. From New Zealand, Rocket Lab’s 98th Electron put three HawkEye 360 satellites into orbit.

beats.title: MAGA / MAHA promises kept
beats.headline: Iran: deal or strikes; Oleshky truce widens.

stories.headline: Peace through strength: Iran told a deal now, or strikes after the vote
stories.body: The promise was to end Iran’s nuclear threat. The action today: mediators carry a proposal swapping UN inspections for oil waivers, while Trump says the job will be finished “through a deal or another way.” The real impact so far is a reopened Hormuz route and an Iranian economy under heavy strain, but also the risk of a new week-long air campaign. Supporters call it leverage; critics fear escalation without a clear end.

stories.headline: Ending the Ukraine war: Oleshky truce widens; talks eyed by Nov. 10
stories.body: The White House-brokered truce has held two days and now covers more of Kherson, and Zelenskyy expects talks in Abu Dhabi by Nov. 10. The impact is concrete for about 2,000 people still in Oleshky, though fighting goes on elsewhere and no evacuation has been confirmed yet.

stories.headline: Lower costs and energy dominance: the methane rule ends
stories.body: Promise: cut regulations and unleash American energy. Action: the President announced the end of the Biden methane rule for oil and gas wells, in a Lubbock rally speech. Impact: the President claims 45 billion dollars in savings and 210 million more barrels; the rule had been projected to prevent 58 million tons of methane by 2038. Supporters see cheaper energy, and critics like EDF call it a “free pass” for polluters.

stories.headline: Ending the Ukraine war: Oleshky truce, day two
stories.body: Promise: end the war. Action: the First Lady’s local ceasefire in Oleshky passed 30 hours without an incident, and the President says he hopes to meet Putin and Zelenskyy soon. Impact: a real, if small, humanitarian opening; skeptics note a missile and 88 drones hit elsewhere in Ukraine the same night.

stories.headline: Peace through strength: Iran strikes after the midterms?
stories.body: Promise: stop Iran’s nuclear program. Action: per the Wall Street Journal, Gulf allies have been told to expect a “short, intense” campaign after Nov. 3, while Gulf states race to finish a peace deal that would reopen Hormuz. Impact: supporters say pressure is pushing Iran toward terms; critics warn of a wider war and higher fuel prices.

stories.headline: MAHA and recovery: Kennedy in Detroit for the STREETS program
stories.body: Promise: treat homelessness and addiction as problems to heal, not manage. Action: Secretary Kennedy visited Detroit, one of eight STREETS communities, each getting 3 million dollars a year for four years for street-based treatment, recovery and housing; Miami-Dade County is another. Impact: the Michigan Advance notes he promoted faith-based recovery after controversy over earlier remarks about Arab Americans. Results will be measured in people housed and sober, not announcements.

stories.headline: MAHA: the breast cancer screening push, one day on
stories.body: Promise: prevention and early detection. Action: HHS’s new effort spreads proven screening and follow-up practices through more than 40 health systems and adds breast-density education. Impact: hospital groups welcomed it; the number to watch is how quickly women get follow-up after an abnormal mammogram.

beats.title: Musk world
beats.headline: Tesla $404.22; SPCX dips; xAI home buyouts in Mississippi.

stories.headline: Tesla eases 0.8 percent to $404.22; SpaceX slips 2.3 percent
stories.body: Tesla gave back a little of Monday and Tuesday’s rally, closing at $404.22, down $3.24, after trading between about $397 and $411. SpaceX (SPCX) fell 2.25 percent to $145.23. Investors are still digesting SpaceX’s roughly 40 billion dollar, five-year deal to lease Nvidia Vera Rubin chips through Apollo, with deliveries starting in early 2027.

stories.headline: xAI offers to buy Mississippi homes from neighbors who won’t sue
stories.body: The Guardian reports agents for xAI, now part of SpaceX, are offering to buy homes in Southaven’s Colonial Hills on the condition owners don’t join a lawsuit over turbine noise; one resident was told the target is 418 homes, and five have sold since Oct. 9. The mayor calls it a goodwill gesture and says city monitors found no noise-limit breach. The company denies the lawsuit’s claims and plans a permanent gas plant by next summer.
stories.why: Local pushback is a growing cost for the data-center buildout that underpins SpaceX’s AI revenue.

stories.headline: Tesla: closed at $407.46, then the Robotaxi fleet passed 1,000 in Texas
stories.body: Tesla rose 4 percent Tuesday to 407.46 dollars and traded near 408 overnight. Benzinga reports 1,051 Robotaxis in Austin, with Cybercabs (544) now outnumbering Model Ys (507). After Governor DeSantis asked for Miami and Tampa service to include the beaches, Musk replied, “Coming soon.” Tesla’s Miami zone is 31 square miles, against Waymo’s 60.

stories.headline: Tesla: hiring in Vietnam; a Semi fire shuts a California freeway
stories.body: Tesla is “officially coming to Vietnam,” a recruiter posted, listing five management jobs weeks after registering a local subsidiary of about 3 million dollars, in a market where VinFast holds about 36 percent of car sales. Less happily, a Tesla Semi fire shut Interstate 880 in Hayward, California. BlackRock’s stake has slipped below 5 percent through dilution.

stories.headline: SpaceX: SPCX up 1.1 percent to $148.58
stories.body: SpaceX shares closed Tuesday at 148.58 dollars, up 1.14 percent. Investors are weighing the 40-billion-dollar AI-chip financing for its AI unit, the former xAI, and Bloomberg’s report that the committees studying a Tesla merger are stacked with Musk allies. Starship Flight 15 is targeted for Nov. 8.

stories.headline: Starlink: next launch Friday morning from California
stories.body: The next Falcon 9 Starlink mission, Group 15-18, is set for early Friday, Oct. 30, from Vandenberg. No SpaceX launch is scheduled today.

beats.title: Space
beats.headline: Electron’s 98th flight; Starship Flight 15 eyes Nov. 8.

stories.headline: Rocket Lab’s 98th Electron puts three HawkEye 360 satellites in orbit
stories.body: Rocket Lab launched “We’re Not Hawking Around” from New Zealand, placing three radio-signal-tracking satellites in a 520-kilometer orbit. It was Rocket Lab’s 19th launch of 2026, with the 100th Electron flight now in sight.

stories.headline: Starship Flight 15 targets Nov. 8 with two catches planned
stories.body: SpaceX aims to catch both the Super Heavy booster and the ship on Flight 15. A ship catch would be a first and is central to making Starship fully reusable, which NASA’s 2028 lunar landing plans depend on.

stories.headline: China’s Guowang network keeps growing
stories.body: Saturday’s Long March 8A from Hainan added nine satellites to Guowang, China’s state broadband answer to Starlink; it was the 674th Long March flight. Next on the U.S. side: Starlink 15-18 from Vandenberg early Friday.

beats.title: NASA
beats.headline: Solar-array spacewalk Thursday; SLS core stage stacks.

stories.headline: Thursday’s spacewalk: Menon and Kutryk to install a new solar array
stories.body: NASA’s Anil Menon and Canada’s Joshua Kutryk step outside Thursday at 8 a.m. Eastern, with NASA+ coverage from 6:30, to install a roll-out solar array on the station’s port truss. Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney will assist from inside. The crew also packed a failed robot-arm wrist joint to ride home on a Dragon in November.

stories.headline: Artemis III: SLS core stage joins the boosters this week
stories.body: NASA said its core stage would be stacked between the twin boosters this week in the Vehicle Assembly Building. A shortened “stubby” stack will do fueling tests to fix past hydrogen leaks, and a stretched Centaur V is the chosen future upper stage. Artemis III, set for no earlier than summer 2027, will test docking with both Blue Origin’s and SpaceX’s landers in Earth orbit, and Axiom is developing a lighter “sortie” suit for two-hour moonwalks, with two paths kept open for a 2028 landing.

stories.headline: UVEX approved; Mars-simulation crew comes out Saturday
stories.body: NASA confirmed the 590-million-dollar UVEX telescope, which will make the first deep ultraviolet maps of the whole sky, for launch by January 2031. On Halloween, the four CHAPEA volunteers leave their 3D-printed Mars habitat in Houston after 378 days.

stories.headline: Swift’s mission ends after almost 22 years
stories.body: After a failed robotic rescue, the Swift observatory, built for two years, will reenter in the coming weeks after catching more than 2,000 gamma-ray bursts and feeding about 7,000 papers.

beats.title: Catholic
beats.headline: Wenski’s Red Mass; Pope thanks Chicago migrant ministers.

stories.headline: Miami: Archbishop Wenski at the Red Mass: “Following Jesus is not for wimps”
stories.body: At Broward’s Red Mass at St. Anthony in Fort Lauderdale, Archbishop Thomas Wenski asked judges and lawyers to see “past the docket numbers” to the human person. He warned that religious liberty is squeezed from the secular left, through mandates, and from the ideological right, by attempts to override internal Church governance. He reminded them the Holy Spirit is the Paraclete, the Advocate, “not parakeet,” as confirmation kids sometimes hear.

stories.headline: Miami: Jericho 2026 continues in Little Haiti
stories.body: The week of renewal Archbishop Wenski opened on his 76th birthday at Notre Dame d’Haïti continues in Little Haiti. In Creole he preached that dignity comes from God, “not TPS or a green card,” and named pride, indifference and fear as walls to be torn down by prayer and the Word. Miami-Dade County, meanwhile, is one of eight communities receiving federal STREETS money for homeless outreach and recovery.

stories.headline: Miami: The archbishop stands firm on school vaccine rules
stories.body: Archbishop Wenski continues to resist Attorney General James Uthmeier’s pressure over religious exemptions in Catholic schools, calling it “bullying” and defending vaccination as serving the common good.

stories.headline: North America: Pope thanks Chicago ministers to detained migrants
stories.body: Pope Leo greeted Chicago’s Coalition for Spiritual and Public Leadership, which ministers daily at the Broadview ICE facility, and posed for a photo with the group. Tiffany Swann-Covington of Our Lady of Africa Parish thanked him for words that “inspired us and countless Bishops.”

stories.headline: Rome: The Pope says faith must become culture
stories.body: At this morning’s audience, Pope Leo quoted Saint John Paul II, saying Christians must pair their faith with patient study and that the Church draws what is good, beautiful and true from every culture.

stories.headline: Africa: The continent now has more Catholics than Europe
stories.body: New Fides figures put Africa’s Catholics at 288.3 million against Europe’s 287.2 million. Africa added 7.58 million Catholics and 1,676 priests, and was the only continent where seminarians increased, by 786, as the world total fell by 2,891. Bishops including Archbishop Ignatius Kaigama of Abuja and Bishop Joseph Kacou Aka of Yamoussoukro are calling for transparent budgets, audits and local giving to sustain that growth.

stories.headline: Asia: Tagbilaran’s new bishop: “Let Bohol welcome the world” without losing itself
stories.body: At his installation, Bishop Crispin Varquez urged tourism that protects Bohol’s environment, workers and heritage, and told his people, “Allow me to love you.” Who he is: a Tagbilaran native, bishop of Borongan for 19 years through Typhoon Yolanda, now the diocese’s eighth bishop, with the motto “Humility and Simplicity.” Cardinal Jose Advincula preached, and about 50 bishops attended.

stories.headline: Europe: Sicily buries Cardinal Paolo Romeo today
stories.body: Who he was: a priest of Acireale who became a Vatican diplomat, nuncio in Haiti, Colombia, Canada and Italy, then archbishop of Palermo from 2006 to 2015; Benedict XVI made him a cardinal in 2010. He died Sunday at 88.

stories.headline: Latin America: The Pope will meet abuse survivors on his trip
stories.body: The Nov. 6–17 visit to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru now includes a meeting with survivors, as Montevideo, Luján, Chiclayo and Cuzco prepare.

stories.headline: Appointments this week: Madagascar, Joliet, Italy and Greece
stories.body: Archbishop Jean Nicolas Rakotojaona now leads Fianarantsoa, Madagascar; born in 1973 with a theology doctorate from Fribourg, he was coadjutor until Sunday. Bishop Brendan Cahill, until now bishop of Victoria, Texas, is installed in Joliet on Nov. 11. Thursday, Giorgio Ferretti takes possession of Lucera-Troia in Italy; Saturday, Georgios Altouvas is installed at Syros in Greece, and Michele Di Tolve, a Milan priest, at Chioggia.

beats.title: Signs of the times
beats.headline: Countdown still Oct. 27; Medjugorje Oct. 25; Moscow and Abu Dhabi.

stories.headline: Countdown to the Kingdom: checked this evening, latest post is still Oct. 27
stories.body: The newest post on Countdown to the Kingdom remains Tuesday’s “How to Offer Your Ordinary Acts in the Divine Will,” drawing on Servant of God Luisa Piccarreta: before ordinary tasks, say interiorly, “Jesus wants to do this in me.” Ahead of it on the page sit Marija’s Oct. 25 Medjugorje message, “A Fire of Hatred is Spreading,” and two Oct. 20–21 messages attributed to Pedro Regis, of Anguera, Brazil, warning of “a great war” and of “the one who opposes Christ.” Pedro’s messages have not been approved by the Church, and the site itself asks readers to test everything with the Church.

stories.headline: Medjugorje, Oct. 25 (latest): “Pray more strongly and more for the peace”
stories.body: The latest monthly message, given Oct. 25, 2026, through Marija: “A fire of hatred and wars is spreading in the hearts of people who do not want peace but their own weak interests. That is why, little children, you be prayer and my extended hands of love and peace for all those who are far from my motherly heart. Pray more strongly and more for the peace that God desires to give you but you do not want it. I am with you and I am praying that peace may prevail and reign in every heart.” The next monthly message is due Nov. 25.

stories.headline: Reading the day beside the message: Moscow, Abu Dhabi and Doha
stories.body: Our Lady’s Oct. 25 message asked for prayer “for the peace that God desires to give.” By evening, the day’s diplomacy fit that request in three places: Putin hosted Ethiopia’s Abiy, with Eritrea’s Isaias due Friday in the same city; Zelenskyy said three-way talks in Abu Dhabi could come by Nov. 10 as the Oleshky truce widened; and Qatar-led mediators pressed Iran toward inspections to avert new strikes. None of these is peace yet. Each is a concrete intention for tonight’s Rosary.

stories.headline: Missions: Africa’s Church overtakes Europe’s
stories.body: Fides counts 288 million Catholics in Africa, now more than in Europe, with Africa the only continent where seminarians increased. For a Church once evangelized by European missionaries, it is a striking reversal. Its bishops say the next test is sustaining that growth honestly, with budgets, audits and local generosity.

stories.headline: Revival on campus: 35 baptized at Ohio State; UniteUS keeps moving
stories.body: Nearly 1,000 people came to Ohio State’s fall kickoff, where 35 were baptized. UniteUS, which began at Auburn in 2023, reported more than 700 decisions for Christ and about 100 baptisms, some in plastic-lined truck beds, at Appalachian State, and held a campus night at South Alabama Tuesday; Belmont in Nashville is next, on Nov. 10. Local churches, not one big organization, are carrying much of this.

stories.headline: Eucharistic: Guatemala’s Cuilapa Host still under study
stories.body: In Cuilapa, a consecrated Host that witnesses say stayed intact in water for eight days and developed reddish stains is being examined by a multidisciplinary team. The diocese stresses only the Holy See can authorize veneration; cases like Sokółka in Poland took years of review.

stories.headline: Digital money, soberly: the digital euro pilot signs up merchants
stories.body: The European Central Bank’s deadline for merchants to apply for its digital euro pilot closed Oct. 27. The 12-month pilot is planned from late 2027, while lawmakers still argue over offline payments, anti-money-laundering rules and fees. In Britain, the national ID card is scrapped but the government digital wallet goes on. These are real systems worth watching closely, with privacy the key question, not cause for panic.

beats.headline: Trunk-or-treats tonight; VOUS free Thursday; Crowder Monday.

stories.headline: Halloween week: trunk-or-treats tonight through Saturday
stories.body: Tonight at 6, Miami-Dade Schools Police holds a free trunk-or-treat at 3300 NW 27th Ave. Thursday from 4 to 8, Hialeah Cares hosts a free party at Miami Dade College Hialeah. Friday and Saturday bring Boo at the Patch at The Berry Farm in Homestead. Saturday afternoon brings Trick-or-Treat on the Mile in Coral Gables, plus Boo in Bloom at Fruit and Spice Park from 10 to 5 and Frost Science’s Spooky Science Monster Mash from 11 to 3.

stories.headline: Thursday: VOUS Worship’s “Man Alive,” free at Bayfront Park
stories.body: VOUS Worship brings “Man Alive” to the FPL Solar Amphitheater on Thursday, Oct. 29. Doors open at 6, music runs 7 to 10, and admission is free.

stories.headline: Next week and beyond: Crowder, Miles Minnick, Gilberto Daza, Jekalyn Carr
stories.body: Crowder and Rend Collective play First Baptist Fort Lauderdale on Monday, Nov. 2. Miles Minnick’s Christlike University Tour stops in Miami Nov. 5. Gilberto Daza’s “Buenas Noticias” tour reaches Hialeah Nov. 14, and Jekalyn Carr and Anthony Brown play the Miramar Cultural Center Nov. 20 at 8.

beats.title: Pick-me-up
beats.headline: Heat at Atlanta now; Eva Mendes joins Starfighter.

stories.headline: Heat at Atlanta right now, chasing a first win
stories.body: The 0–4 Heat tipped off at 7 at State Farm Arena against the 2–2 Hawks, who were 3.5-point favorites and without Mouhamed Gueye (foot). Giannis Antetokounmpo comes in off his first Heat triple-double, 29 points, 15 rebounds and 11 assists, in the 113–109 loss to Dallas. Next up: Indiana at Kaseya Center Friday at 8.

stories.headline: Star Wars: Eva Mendes reportedly joins Ryan Gosling in Starfighter
stories.body: Eva Mendes is expected to play Belle, a glamorous cantina owner, in Star Wars: Starfighter, opposite her husband Ryan Gosling, ComicBook.com reports; Lucasfilm has not confirmed it. Gosling plays Kade Auberon in Shawn Levy’s film, which opens May 28, 2027.

stories.headline: Star Wars: Episode X reportedly built around two new leads
stories.body: Reports say Episode X, reportedly to be directed by Jon Watts, centers on two new leads, with Daisy Ridley’s Rey in a mentoring role. Lucasfilm hasn’t confirmed details. Ahsoka Season 2 arrives Jan. 20, 2027 on Disney+.
