beats.title: Catholic
beats.headline: Wenski on dignity; Varquez installed in Bohol; Nigerian priest freed.

stories.headline: Miami: Archbishop Wenski at Jericho 2026: “God gave us our dignity”
stories.body: Celebrating his 76th birthday at Notre Dame d’Haïti in Little Haiti, Archbishop Thomas Wenski preached in Haitian Creole at the opening of Jericho, the mission’s week of renewal. “It is not TPS or a green card that gives us dignity,” he said; “God made us human.” He named walls of pride, indifference and fear, and the fear of ICE, to be torn down by prayer and the Word, not violence. Haiti’s TPS ended in July and legal challenges continue.

stories.headline: Miami: The archdiocese holds firm on school vaccine rules
stories.body: Archbishop Wenski continues to resist Attorney General James Uthmeier’s pressure over religious exemptions in Catholic schools, calling it “bullying” and defending vaccination as serving the common good.

stories.headline: Europe: Assisi’s 40th-anniversary peace prayer closes today
stories.body: Christian leaders gather this afternoon in the Lower Basilica of Saint Francis, with Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew speaking and Pope Leo’s message read in his absence. The theme, “Disarmed and Disarming Peace,” is the title of the Pope’s July book.

stories.headline: Asia: Bishop Crispin Varquez installed in his hometown, Tagbilaran
stories.body: Bishop Crispin “Bai” Varquez took possession of the Diocese of Tagbilaran in Bohol, Philippines, this morning as its eighth bishop, urging “passion and enthusiasm for the work of evangelization.” Who he is: a Tagbilaran native, 65, ordained in 1989, a former seminary formator, and bishop of Borongan in Eastern Samar from 2007. He succeeds Alberto Uy, now archbishop of Cebu.

stories.headline: Africa: Kidnapped Nigerian priest freed in Benue
stories.body: Fr. John Inalegwu Otache, pastor of St. Margaret’s in Ajegbe-Awume, was rescued with seven other captives by Benue police and local vigilantes, and two suspects were arrested. The Diocese of Otukpo gave thanks “with hearts full of joy” and asked prayers for those still held, including Fr. Emmanuel Ezema of Zaria, missing since December.

stories.headline: Middle East: Jordan answers the Karak church attack with strikes in Syria
stories.body: After Friday’s attack on a funeral at St. George Orthodox Church in Hamoud, Jordan struck Islamic State targets in southern Syria and says it killed more than 20 fighters. Syria reports eight civilian deaths. Pope Leo prayed for the victims at Sunday’s Angelus.

stories.headline: North America: New York’s $800 million abuse settlement nears signing
stories.body: The Archdiocese of New York and about 1,300 survivors agreed to an 800-million-dollar settlement, to be signed the week of Nov. 6. Archbishop Ronald Hicks prayed it would “bring some measure of healing and reconciliation.”

stories.headline: Latin America: Peru, Argentina and Uruguay prepare for the Pope
stories.body: With the Pope’s medical all-clear, preparations go ahead for Nov. 6–17, from Montevideo and Luján to Chiclayo, where he was bishop, and Cuzco.

stories.headline: Appointments this week: Madagascar, Joliet, Italy and Greece
stories.body: Archbishop Jean Nicolas Rakotojaona now leads Fianarantsoa, Madagascar. He was born in 1973, holds a theology doctorate from Fribourg and was coadjutor until Sunday. Bishop Brendan Cahill, until now bishop of Victoria, Texas, will be installed in Joliet on Nov. 11. Thursday, Giorgio Ferretti takes possession of Lucera-Troia in Italy. Saturday, Georgios Altouvas is installed at Syros in Greece, and Michele Di Tolve, a Milan priest, at Chioggia.

beats.title: Signs of the times
beats.headline: Medjugorje Oct. 25; Countdown Oct. 25; campus revival tonight.

stories.headline: Medjugorje, Oct. 25: “Pray more strongly and more for the peace”
stories.body: The latest monthly message, given Oct. 25, 2026, through the visionary Marija: “Dear children! A fire of hatred and wars is spreading in the hearts of people who do not want peace but their own weak interests. That is why, little children, you be prayer and my extended hands of love and peace for all those who are far from my motherly heart. Pray more strongly and more for the peace that God desires to give you but you do not want it. I am with you and I am praying that peace may prevail and reign in every heart.” The next monthly message is due Nov. 25.

stories.headline: Countdown to the Kingdom: latest post Oct. 25
stories.body: Checked this morning, the newest post is still Sunday, Oct. 25: “Marija – A Fire of Hatred is Spreading,” summed up as “Pray for people who do not want peace.” Before it came “The Suicide of the West” and “Defending Your Family” on Oct. 23, and two messages attributed to Pedro Regis: “The One Who Opposes Christ” on Oct. 21 and “There Will be a Great War” on Oct. 20. The site asks readers to test every message with the Church, which alone judges authenticity.

stories.headline: The message and the night’s news, read together
stories.body: In the 48 hours since Our Lady spoke of a “fire of hatred and wars,” 16 ballistic missiles fell on Kyiv, Houthi missiles flew at Saudi cities, Jordan struck Syria over a church massacre, and El Fasher marked a year under the RSF. Against that, religious leaders from 53 nations pray in Assisi today, and a small truce lets aid reach Oleshky. The message asks for two things: be prayer, and be “extended hands of love and peace.” Jesus’ words in Matthew 24 still apply: “See that you are not alarmed.”

stories.headline: Revival on campus: UniteUS reaches South Alabama tonight
stories.body: UniteUS, the student outreach that began at Auburn in 2023, holds its next campus night tonight at the University of South Alabama. At Appalachian State this month it reported more than 700 decisions for Christ and about 100 baptisms. The ministry says it has reached more than two dozen campuses, the University of Miami among them, and more than 100,000 students. Belmont in Nashville is next, on Nov. 10.

stories.headline: Revival by the water: beach and campus baptisms keep spreading
stories.body: More than 550 people were baptized at Bridlington South Beach in England on Oct. 10, after earlier beach baptisms at Bigbury. Thousands joined the oceanfront baptisms at Oceanside, California, on Oct. 17. Local churches report students baptized after campus nights from Mississippi to Georgia. Many of these gatherings are led by local congregations, not one big organization.

stories.headline: Eucharistic: Guatemala’s Cuilapa Host under study
stories.body: Witnesses in Cuilapa, Guatemala, describe a consecrated Host that stayed intact in water for eight days and developed reddish stains. A multidisciplinary team is studying it, and the diocese stresses that only the Holy See can authorize veneration. Similar cases, such as Sokółka in Poland, took years of scientific and Church review.

stories.headline: Digital ID, soberly: Britain dropped the scheme but kept the plumbing
stories.body: Britain has scrapped its national digital ID card, the compulsory-then-voluntary plan that Prime Minister Andy Burnham ended. But officials told MPs that One Login and the government digital wallet continue, with more than 80 credential types planned and digital driving licences targeted for 2027. One MP warned of digital ID “by the back door.” In Europe, the digital euro is still being negotiated, with a pilot planned for late 2027 and possible issuance in 2029. It is real infrastructure that deserves scrutiny, not panic.

beats.title: Miami
beats.headline: Halloween week events; VOUS free Thursday; Crowder Monday.

stories.headline: This week: trunk-or-treats and family Halloween nights
stories.body: Wednesday at 6 p.m. Miami-Dade Schools Police holds a free trunk-or-treat at 3300 NW 27th Ave. Thursday from 4 to 8, Hialeah Cares throws a free Halloween party and haunted house at Miami Dade College Hialeah. On Friday, The Berry Farm hosts Boo at the Patch from 3 p.m. Saturday brings Trick-or-Treat on the Mile in Coral Gables from 2 to 6, Frost Science’s Spooky Science Monster Mash from 11 to 3, and Tidal Cove’s “Tidal-ween.”

stories.headline: Thursday: VOUS Worship’s “Man Alive,” free at Bayfront Park
stories.body: VOUS Worship brings “Man Alive” to the FPL Solar Amphitheater at Bayfront Park on Thursday, Oct. 29. Doors open at 6, music runs 7 to 10, and admission is free.

stories.headline: Next week and beyond: Crowder, Miles Minnick, Gilberto Daza, Jekalyn Carr
stories.body: Crowder and Rend Collective play First Baptist Fort Lauderdale on Monday, Nov. 2. Miles Minnick’s Christlike University Tour stops in Miami on Nov. 5, the same day the Braveheart men’s summit opens at One Name Church. Gilberto Daza’s “Buenas Noticias” tour reaches Hialeah Nov. 14. Gospel artists Jekalyn Carr and Anthony Brown play the Miramar Cultural Center on Friday, Nov. 20, at 8.

beats.title: Pick-me-up
beats.headline: Giannis triple-double in loss; Ahsoka trailer brings back Anakin.

stories.headline: Heat: Giannis’s first Miami triple-double, but Flagg’s block sinks them
stories.body: Giannis Antetokounmpo had 29 points, 15 rebounds and 11 assists, his first triple-double with the Heat, and Davion Mitchell scored 21. But Cooper Flagg had 29 points and 11 assists, and with 31 seconds left he blocked Andrew Wiggins’s three that would have put Miami ahead. Dallas won 113–109. At 0–4, the Heat are off to their worst start since 2008–09. Next: at Atlanta Wednesday at 7, then Indiana at home Friday at 8.
stories.why: In 2008–09, the Heat started 0–4 and still made the playoffs.

stories.headline: Star Wars: Ahsoka Season 2 trailer brings back Hayden Christensen’s Anakin
stories.body: The new trailer, shown at D23, sets Ahsoka Season 2 for Jan. 20, 2027 on Disney+. Anakin returns as a Force ghost and in Clone Wars flashbacks, asking Ahsoka: “Are you a Jedi... or not?” Sabine trains with Ahsoka on Peridea, Ezra fights Death Troopers, and Rory McCann takes over as Baylan Skoll. Dave Filoni says the Mortis gods are “definitely a thing.”

stories.headline: Star Wars: Vader’s Monday Night Football interviews begin
stories.body: An animated Darth Vader began interviewing NFL players on Monday Night Football, building to an all-animated Star Wars telecast of the Super Bowl on Feb. 14, 2027. Next Tuesday, Nov. 3, the 256-page art book for The Mandalorian and Grogu arrives.

label: Monday evening
topLine: Doctors clear Pope Leo for South America; Gulf envoys meet in Tehran; Tesla jumps 5%; the Heat host Dallas at 7:30.

newAtThisHour.headline: Doctors clear Pope Leo for his Nov. 6–17 South America trip
newAtThisHour.body: The Vatican says there are no medical obstacles; the full program, including Cuzco, stands.

newAtThisHour.headline: Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani envoys meet Iran’s leaders in Tehran
newAtThisHour.body: They sought to avert a return to war as Egypt authorized military help for Saudi Arabia.

newAtThisHour.headline: Zelenskyy says three-way peace talks restart in November
newAtThisHour.body: Russia says it will keep attacking but could accept local humanitarian truces.

newAtThisHour.headline: Kenya releases 20 Ebola contacts; Uganda tightens Congo border
newAtThisHour.body: Kenya’s nine cases remain in one cluster with no community spread.

newAtThisHour.headline: The President calls Brazil’s vote “rigged,” without evidence
newAtThisHour.body: Brazil’s electoral court confirmed Lula’s 51.8 percent win.

newAtThisHour.headline: Tesla closes up 5.2 percent after a Barclays upgrade
newAtThisHour.body: Barclays cites an expected SpaceX merger; SpaceX also closed a 40-billion-dollar chip financing deal.

newAtThisHour.headline: More than 250 hospitals sign the MAHA hospital food pledge
newAtThisHour.body: Secretary Kennedy announced it in Grand Rapids.

beats.title: World
beats.headline: Pope cleared to travel; Tehran talks; Ukraine talks in November.

stories.headline: Vatican City: Doctors clear Pope Leo for his Nov. 6–17 South America trip
stories.body: The Vatican said Monday that, based on the Pope’s clinical status and recent tests, there are no contraindications to his apostolic journey to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, which will go ahead as published. That includes high-altitude Cuzco, above 11,000 feet, less than four weeks after surgeons removed the lower lobe of his right lung on Oct. 13. The 12-day trip covers 10 cities and 14 flights.
stories.why: It answers the biggest question hanging over the pontificate this month: whether his recovery would allow the long journey home to the continent where he served as a missionary.

stories.headline: Vatican City: Pope receives Slovenia’s president; Mongolia’s cardinal visits
stories.body: Pope Leo received Slovenian President Nataša Pirc Musar this morning; talks with Cardinal Parolin and Archbishop Gallagher then turned to the Western Balkans, Ukraine and the Middle East. He also received Cardinal Giorgio Marengo, who leads the small Church in Mongolia, and told the Sisters of Charity of Saint Jeanne-Antide Thouret, in their founder’s bicentenary year, to care for the whole person, body and soul. A papal telegram mourned Cardinal Paolo Romeo.

stories.headline: Vatican City: Cardinal Paolo Romeo, Palermo’s former archbishop, dies at 88
stories.body: Cardinal Paolo Romeo, archbishop of Palermo from 2006 to 2015 and earlier a papal nuncio on several continents, died Sunday at San Marco Hospital in Catania. His funeral is Wednesday, Oct. 28, at 11 a.m. in the cathedral of Acireale, his home diocese. Sunday’s Holy See bulletin also carried the Angelus and new appointments, including a succession in Madagascar.

stories.headline: Africa: Kenya frees 20 Ebola contacts; Nigeria’s patient flown to Switzerland
stories.body: Twenty contacts of Kenya’s first Bundibugyo Ebola patient went home Monday after 21 symptom-free days; 98 remain in quarantine, and Kenya counts nine cases and two deaths, all in one family-and-caregiver cluster with no community spread. Nigeria’s only case, the Ugandan-born wife of a Swiss diplomat, was flown from Abuja to Switzerland and is stable. Uganda now admits only essential travelers from Congo, where the outbreak has passed 9,960 confirmed cases.
stories.why: WHO advises screening rather than travel bans; Uganda’s stricter border shows how nervous neighbors are about an outbreak now approaching 10,000 confirmed cases.

stories.headline: Africa: Sudan’s army steps up airstrikes in Darfur and Kordofan
stories.body: On the anniversary of El Fasher’s fall, Sudan’s army intensified air and drone strikes on Rapid Support Forces positions around El Fasher and in Kordofan. Amnesty says fewer than 70,000 people remain in the city, facing detention, torture and little aid. In North Kordofan, the army and allied forces have advanced since September, but El Obeid still lives under RSF drone fire and near-siege conditions.

stories.headline: Africa: Fighting grinds on in South Kivu despite Swiss-hosted talks
stories.body: The M23-aligned coalition says it seized a strategic hill in South Kivu after five days of fighting, as government forces answered with drones and mortars around Walungu. In North Kivu, an attack near Nyamilima killed a wildlife-monitoring worker. U.S. envoy Massad Boulos has praised progress between Kinshasa and the AFC/M23 after talks in Switzerland, but the front lines have not quieted.

stories.headline: Asia: Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani envoys meet Iran’s leaders in Tehran
stories.body: Delegations from the three Mecca defense pact nations met Iranian leaders Monday to head off a return to war, and discussed the Houthis’ attacks on Saudi Arabia. Saudi forces said they shot down another Houthi missile aimed at Riyadh and destroyed two launchers in Sanaa, while Egypt’s parliament authorized military support for the kingdom. CNN reports U.S. forces could launch a major operation within 96 hours of an order, though the President has not decided.

stories.headline: Asia: Israel votes Tuesday in its first election since Oct. 7
stories.body: Israelis go to the polls tomorrow in a fragmented race where no bloc is projected to reach 61 seats, so coalition bargaining will likely decide whether Benjamin Netanyahu stays in office. His main challenger is former army chief Gadi Eisenkot. Official results are due Nov. 4.

stories.headline: Asia: Jordan captures all three church-attack suspects after a shootout
stories.body: Jordanian security forces arrested all three men suspected of Friday’s attack on a funeral at St. George Greek Orthodox Church in Hamoud, Karak. The arrests came this morning after a roughly three-hour gunfight at an abandoned house, and all three were wounded. The attack killed eight people and wounded about 40, and 27 remain in hospital. King Abdullah promised the “harshest penalties.” Jordan is home to about 300,000 Christians among 11.5 million people, and attacks like this are rare there.

stories.headline: Europe: Zelenskyy says three-way talks restart in November
stories.body: Volodymyr Zelenskyy said U.S.-Ukraine-Russia talks will resume in November and that territorial questions can be discussed there. Moscow said it will not slow its offensive but is open to local “humanitarian” ceasefires. Zelenskyy also complained of a month-long wait for Pentagon sign-off on Patriot interceptors, while a Ukrainian drone attack on Russia’s Voronezh region killed at least two people and Kyiv says it hit a missile-battery plant in Yelets.

stories.headline: Europe: France counts 1,314 arrests; Italy marches under military guard
stories.body: Final figures from Saturday’s cost-of-living protests in France: 1,314 arrests, 53 police injured, 75 fires and 24 shops looted. Officials counted 410,000 marchers nationwide; unions said 800,000. About 70,000 security personnel were deployed, and the interior ministry defended the operation. On Sunday it was Italy’s turn. Milan’s centre was guarded by 500 extra soldiers and some 5,000 police, the march was largely peaceful, and there were nine arrests nationwide.

stories.headline: Europe: EU plans new deportation powers for Frontex
stories.body: Euronews reports the EU will let its border agency move migrants between countries outside Europe, extending its work to so-called return hubs. Separately, Cyprus signed a 1.8-billion-dollar deal to develop its first gas field, with exports to Europe through Egypt from 2028.

stories.headline: North America: The President says Brazil’s vote looked “rigged”
stories.body: The President said Lula’s win “looked like another rigged election,” offering no evidence. Brazil’s electoral court confirmed Lula with 51.79 percent to Flávio Bolsonaro’s 48.21 percent, a margin of about 4.4 million votes, while Bolsonaro asked for the result to be annulled.

stories.headline: North America: Early vote passes 26 million with eight days to go
stories.body: About 26 to 27 million Americans had voted early by Sunday. Georgia set a first-day record of more than 188,000 ballots, 40 percent above 2022, and Dallas County cast 76,069 on its first day. Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3. In Florida, early voting is under way statewide through Saturday.

stories.headline: North America: In Port Huron, the President promises $5,000 checks
stories.body: President Trump held a rally in Port Huron, Michigan, on Sunday, the first visit by a sitting president to the city. He backed Mike Rogers for the Senate and John James for governor, and attacked Democrats Abdul El-Sayed and Jocelyn Benson. He said every adult citizen would get $5,000 if Republicans hold both chambers. Benson answered that “Michigan citizens will have the final say on November 3rd.” Former President Obama campaigned in Detroit on Saturday.

stories.headline: South America: Lula wins a fourth term in a historic comeback
stories.body: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won Sunday’s runoff with 51.79 percent to Flávio Bolsonaro’s 48.21 percent, a margin of about 4.4 million votes. He is the first candidate to win after trailing in the first round, which Flávio had led 47 to 45. Turnout was 80.8 percent, and voting was extended two hours because of transport failures. Flávio refused to concede and says he will seek to annul the result. Electoral court judges said overnight there are no grounds to do so and denied his claim that his party’s monitors were removed from the counting room. Lula is inaugurated Jan. 5.
stories.why: Brazil’s bishops had asked voters to respect the ballot box. How Flávio’s side handles defeat this week will test that.

stories.headline: South America: Machado offers to sit down with Delcy Rodríguez
stories.body: A day after returning from exile, María Corina Machado said she is ready to meet acting president Delcy Rodríguez, with transparency and a defined agenda. Rodríguez did not confirm Machado a seat at the talks but said dialogue should make room for all voices. The EU welcomed Machado’s return and called for free and fair elections, while Washington has avoided naming a date.

stories.headline: South America: Pope Leo’s November journey stays on the calendar
stories.body: Despite the Pope’s surgery, the Vatican and local organizers say the Nov. 6–17 trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru goes ahead. Stops include Montevideo, Buenos Aires, Luján and Córdoba, then Lima, Chiclayo, Cusco and Pucallpa. In Peru Pope Leo served as a missionary and bishop for more than 20 years.

stories.headline: Oceania: Parliament honours Helen Haines, now serious but stable
stories.body: Australia’s Parliament returned this morning under tighter security, with tributes to independent MP Helen Haines, who lost both legs in an alleged deliberate car attack outside her Wangaratta office. MPs wore orange heart pins, and Prime Minister Anthony Albanese warned against a rising “normalisation of the language of grievance and violence.” Her colleague Allegra Spender said her first words on waking were concern for her staff and thanks to the bystanders and nurses. She is now in serious but stable condition, and a 43-year-old man has been charged.

stories.headline: Oceania: A 1,500-km storm line lashes New South Wales
stories.body: An unusually large line of thunderstorms, about 1,500 kilometres long, swept through New South Wales and Sydney on Sunday. Camden recorded a gust of 82 km/h and Cabramurra 113 km/h. Flood warnings are in place, and more storms are forecast this week.

stories.headline: Oceania: New Zealand opens advance voting
stories.body: Enrolment closed at midnight Sunday, and advance voting opened this morning at 207 locations across New Zealand, with early queues. Election day is Saturday, Nov. 7.

beats.title: MAGA / MAHA promises kept
beats.headline: 250 hospitals sign food pledge; Iran decision looms; new plants.

stories.headline: MAHA: More than 250 hospitals pledge healthier food
stories.body: In Grand Rapids, Secretary Kennedy announced that more than 250 hospitals have signed the Make Hospital Food Healthier pledge, with a recognition badge for those that follow through. He also promoted a push for medical schools to require 40 hours of nutrition training or an equivalent competency. The pledges are voluntary, so the real test is what lands on patients’ trays and in curricula over the next year.

stories.headline: Peace through strength: “decision time” on Iran
stories.body: The President told Fox News he is deciding whether to “finish it off” or “make a deal” with Iran, naming the buried Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site as a possible target. He has said strikes would not resume before the Nov. 3 midterms. Supporters see pressure that brings Tehran to the table; critics fear a wider war that already has Houthi missiles falling on Saudi Arabia.

stories.headline: Bringing back industry: the White House tallies new plants
stories.body: The White House highlighted Audi’s 4.2-billion-dollar Georgia plant, 1.3 billion dollars for fertilizer production in Nebraska, chip expansion in North Carolina and a 6.6-billion-dollar Baltimore shipyard. Announced investment is not the same as jobs filled, and several projects will take years to open. The President also announced a new Chiricahua National Park in Arizona.

stories.headline: Lower gas prices: the White House says relief is coming “rapidly”
stories.body: Promise: cheaper fuel. Action: a White House release on Sunday points to Defense Production Act money for refining, a Venezuela oil deal that has raised Venezuelan imports more than 400 percent, 130 million barrels of diesel released by partner countries, EPA fuel waivers, and a $54 billion Alaska gas pipeline deal with Korea and Taiwan. It also says more oil is leaving Hormuz than before the conflict. Impact so far: not yet at the pump. Brent closed Friday at $116.72, a six-month high, up 6.2 percent for the week. Supporters say supply measures take weeks to work, while critics say the war risk outweighs them.

stories.headline: Affordability: a $5,000 check, if Republicans win both chambers
stories.body: Promise: at Sunday’s Michigan rally, the President said every adult citizen would get $5,000 if Republicans hold the House and Senate. Action: no bill or funding mechanism has been introduced yet. Impact: for now this is a campaign pledge, not policy. Any payment would need Congress to pass it. Supporters call it sharing the tariff and growth dividend, and skeptics point to its cost and the deficit.

stories.headline: Ending the Ukraine war: truce Tuesday, talks in November
stories.body: Promise: end the war in Ukraine. Action: Starlink service is restored, a local truce around Oleshky starts Tuesday, and talks are planned in Abu Dhabi in November. Impact: Russia still fired 140 drones overnight, so the test this week is whether the small truce holds.

stories.headline: Election integrity: record early turnout, eight days out
stories.body: Promise: secure, trusted elections. Impact so far: early turnout is running hot, with 26 million or more ballots cast and Georgia’s first-day record 40 percent above 2022. Both parties are urging supporters to vote early, which both sides once treated with suspicion.

beats.title: Musk world
beats.headline: Tesla jumps 5% on Barclays upgrade; SpaceX’s $40B chip deal.

stories.headline: Tesla: Barclays upgrade sends shares up 5 percent to $391.62
stories.body: Tesla closed at 391.62 dollars, up 5.2 percent, its best day since early September, after Barclays upgraded it to overweight and raised its target to 450 dollars from 370. Barclays says an expected merger with SpaceX is now central to the bull case and also cited a recovering auto business and rising robotaxi miles. Even after Monday, the stock is down about 13 percent this year.

stories.headline: SpaceX: a $40 billion GPU financing deal with Apollo
stories.body: Musk said SpaceX closed a roughly 40-billion-dollar debt deal, backed by Apollo, to lease AI chips starting in early 2027 for its AI unit, the former xAI. He also said many smaller AI cloud providers will fail or consolidate and that SpaceX will not buy them, comments that pushed those stocks lower.

stories.headline: Tesla: Berlin builds a record week; Roadster trims revealed
stories.body: Tesla’s Berlin plant built a record 7,000 Model Ys in one week, against a target of 7,500. New Roadster details list three trims, Performance, Thrust and the invite-only Rocket, with $50,000 and $250,000 reservations and a claimed 0 to 60 time under 0.59 seconds. One analyst, Phillip Securities, still rates the stock Sell with a $230 target, despite third-quarter earnings that beat estimates.

stories.headline: Starlink in Ukraine: Kyiv disputes Musk’s claim of violated terms
stories.body: Ukraine rejects Musk’s claim that it broke Starlink’s terms. Meanwhile service on fast-moving platforms, above 400 km/h, has been restored, which matters for drones. Musk says changes to Starshield, the military version, are controlled by the US government. The episode leaves investors and Kyiv asking how much frontline communication depends on one company’s decisions.

stories.headline: SpaceX: a double upgrade, and Starship eyes November
stories.body: SpaceX, trading as SPCX since its June 12 IPO, ended last week on a rare double analyst upgrade to Buy on AI growth. Its next Starship flight is targeted for November. A filing shows that any Tesla merger would need Musk’s own sign-off. Grok’s new business partner network launched with about 130 partners.

beats.title: Space
beats.headline: Starlink 15-16 tonight; China’s Guowang batch; Starship eyes November.

stories.headline: China’s Long March 8A lofts nine Guowang internet satellites
stories.body: A Long March 8A lifted off from the Hainan commercial launch site at Wenchang at 10:03 p.m. Eastern on Saturday, carrying nine satellites for Guowang, China’s state broadband constellation and its answer to Starlink. It was the 674th flight of the Long March family.

stories.headline: Overnight: Starlink 15-16 from Vandenberg on a 26th-flight booster
stories.body: A Falcon 9 is set to carry 27 Starlink satellites from Vandenberg tonight, with the window opening at 12:45 a.m. Eastern Tuesday. The first-stage booster is flying for the 26th time.

stories.headline: Starship and new pads: November’s big test
stories.body: Starship’s next flight is eyed for November. Blue Origin is planning new Florida pads, and Starbase is seeking approval for up to 456 launches a year. Launch capacity is now the bottleneck for both moon programs.

beats.title: NASA
beats.headline: Spacewalk prep; USDA pact; Perseverance studies Mars dust.

stories.headline: Spacewalk prep and a new moon-landing simulator
stories.body: The station crew spent Monday on robotics work ahead of Thursday’s spacewalk to install a new roll-out solar array. NASA also signed an agreement with the Agriculture Department to use Earth-observation data for crop and hazard monitoring, and invited reporters to a lunar-landing simulator at Ames on Oct. 29–30 as Artemis aims for a 2028 landing.

stories.headline: Perseverance measures Mars dust to protect future crews
stories.body: JPL says Perseverance has measured ultrafine Martian dust, data that will shape how suits, habitats and filters are designed for astronauts. NASA also reported its NEO Surveyor asteroid-hunting telescope now has its sunshade ready.

stories.headline: NASA adopts Apollo’s urgency to build a moon base in two years
stories.body: An AP report this weekend lays out administrator Jared Isaacman’s timeline. Artemis III next summer becomes an Earth-orbit docking test of both commercial landers, SpaceX’s and Blue Origin’s, with three launches in quick succession and an Italian astronaut on board. Artemis IV would land in 2028. The first moon-base cargo flight, Astrobotic’s second try for the south pole, comes by year’s end, and lighter Axiom “sortie suits” will be tested on the space station next year. Isaacman calls it “the same playbook that went from Apollo 7 splashdown to Apollo 11 in just nine months.”
stories.why: Safety advisers have warned that speed must not outrun crew safety. That tension will shape the next year.

stories.headline: Stennis Space Center marks 65 years of rocket testing
stories.body: NASA’s Stennis Space Center in Mississippi, where engines from Saturn V to the Space Launch System were tested, is marking its 65th anniversary.

beats.title: Catholic
beats.headline: Wenski on Haitian families; Pope’s trip confirmed; Tagbilaran bishop.

stories.headline: Miami: Archbishop Wenski dedicates a new altar at La Merced
stories.body: On Saturday Archbishop Thomas Wenski consecrated the new altar of Our Lady of Mercy (La Merced) Mission at Corpus Christi parish. Founded in 2005 under Fr. José Luis Menéndez, the mission is known for hand-carved cedar altars by Bolivian craftsmen, 23-karat gold leaf applied by Cuban conservators, and more than 130 Latin American colonial paintings and sculptures. In his homily the archbishop spoke of the way of beauty, saying “beauty is strictly at the service of evangelization,” and that “here there is a place for all.”
stories.why: For a music minister: the rite of dedication is one of the richest liturgies in the book, and Miami rarely sees one.

stories.headline: Miami: Archbishop Wenski on immigration and the Haitian community
stories.body: In the second part of a WLRN interview released Monday, Archbishop Thomas Wenski spoke about immigration, Temporary Protected Status and the archdiocese’s support for Haitian families. He has long ministered to Haitians, having learned Creole as a young priest in Little Haiti.

stories.headline: Miami: Catholic schools’ vaccine rules fight continues
stories.body: Archbishop Wenski is still pushing back against Attorney General James Uthmeier over vaccine requirements in Catholic schools. The archdiocese says its schools may set their own health standards.

stories.headline: South America: The Pope’s trip home is confirmed
stories.body: For Catholics in Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, Monday’s medical all-clear means preparations go ahead for the Nov. 6–17 visit, including Cuzco. Peru is especially personal for Pope Leo, who served there for years as a missionary and bishop of Chiclayo.

stories.headline: Africa: Madagascar’s Fianarantsoa gets a new archbishop
stories.body: Pope Leo accepted the resignation of Archbishop Fulgence Rabemahafaly of Fianarantsoa, 75, on Sunday. His coadjutor, Jean Nicolas Rakotojaona, succeeds him immediately. Who he is: born in Antananarivo in 1973 and ordained in 2002, he earned a doctorate in theology at Fribourg, led a seminary, and became auxiliary bishop of Morondava in 2023 and coadjutor a year ago.

stories.headline: North America: New York archdiocese agrees to $800 million abuse settlement
stories.body: The Archdiocese of New York and about 1,300 survivors of clergy abuse agreed to an $800 million settlement, the second-largest by a US archdiocese. Archbishop Ronald Hicks told clergy it will be final when signed during the week of Nov. 6 and prayed it would “bring some measure of healing and reconciliation.” Separately, Milwaukee’s Archbishop Jeffrey Grob and Des Moines’ Bishop William Joensen said a White House prayer visit was publicized for politics without their consent.

stories.headline: North America: Indianapolis to host the 2029 Eucharistic Congress
stories.body: The National Eucharistic Congress returns to Indianapolis in 2029, building on the 2024 congress that drew about 50,000 people.

stories.headline: Europe: Italy mourns Cardinal Paolo Romeo
stories.body: Cardinal Paolo Romeo, archbishop of Palermo from 2006 to 2015, died Sunday at 88. Who he was: a Sicilian Vatican diplomat who served as papal nuncio in several countries, including Italy, before Benedict XVI sent him to Palermo. In 2013 he presided over the beatification of Blessed Pino Puglisi, the priest murdered by the mafia. His funeral is Wednesday in Acireale.

stories.headline: Middle East: Christians in Jordan bury their dead as suspects are caught
stories.body: The Orthodox community of Hamoud, near Karak, is mourning those killed in Friday’s funeral attack. Pope Leo prayed for them at the Angelus, and all three suspects were arrested this morning.

stories.headline: Asia: Korea’s bishops elect a new president ahead of Seoul WYD
stories.body: Korea’s bishops elected Bishop Augustine Kim Jong-su of Daejeon as conference president and approved new guidelines on sexual violence in the Church. Who he is: Kim, 70, chaired the bishops’ special committee that drafted those guidelines, and his conference is preparing for World Youth Day in Seoul in 2027. In the Philippines, Bishop Crispin Varquez is installed at Tagbilaran on Tuesday.

stories.headline: Latin America: Brazil’s bishops had asked respect for the ballot box
stories.body: Before Sunday’s runoff, the Brazilian bishops’ Permanent Council defended democracy and a conscientious vote without naming candidates, while 64 bishops signed a separate letter. With Flávio Bolsonaro disputing the result, that call to accept the ballot box now applies.

stories.headline: Appointments: Bishop Varquez installed in Tagbilaran Tuesday; Cahill to Joliet
stories.body: Bishop Crispin Varquez, a native of Bohol who led the Diocese of Borongan in Eastern Samar for 19 years, will be installed Tuesday morning as the eighth bishop of Tagbilaran in the Philippines, with Cardinal Jose Advincula preaching. In Illinois, Cardinal Cupich will join the Nov. 11 installation of Bishop Brendan Cahill, until now bishop of Victoria in Texas, as Joliet’s seventh bishop; he succeeds Archbishop Ronald Hicks, now in New York.

stories.headline: Appointments calendar: installations this week
stories.body: Tuesday, Oct. 27: Crispin Varquez, the former bishop of Borongan, is installed at Tagbilaran in the Philippines. Thursday: Giorgio Ferretti takes possession of Lucera-Troia in Italy. Saturday, Oct. 31: Jean Abou Charouche is ordained Melkite exarch for Argentina, Georgios Altouvas is installed at Syros in Greece, and Michele Di Tolve, a priest of Milan, at Chioggia. Bishop Emeritus Virginio Bressanelli of Neuquén, Argentina, died Oct. 23.

beats.title: Signs of the times
beats.headline: Countdown Oct. 25; Medjugorje Oct. 25; beach baptisms spread.

stories.headline: Medjugorje, Oct. 25: “A fire of hatred and wars is spreading”
stories.body:
Our Lady’s monthly message through the visionary Marija, given Oct. 25, 2026: “Dear children! A fire of hatred and wars is spreading in the hearts of people who do not want peace but their own weak interests. That is why, little children, you be prayer and my extended hands of love and peace for all those who are far from my motherly heart. Pray more strongly and more for the peace that God desires to give you, but you do not want it. I am with you and I am praying that peace may prevail and begin to reign in every heart. Thank you for having responded to my call.”

It came on the same day the Assisi peace meeting opened and the Pope pleaded for Yemen. The Vatican’s 2024 nulla osta encourages the spiritual fruits of Medjugorje without declaring the messages supernatural.
stories.why: The message asks for a response, not fear: be prayer, and be her hands of peace.

stories.headline: Countdown to the Kingdom: latest post Oct. 25
stories.body: The site’s newest post, dated Sunday, Oct. 25, carries the Medjugorje message under the title “Marija – A Fire of Hatred is Spreading.” Earlier posts were “The Suicide of the West” and “Defending Your Family” on Oct. 23, and Pedro Regis messages on Oct. 20 and 21: “There Will be a Great War” and “The One Who Opposes Christ.”

stories.headline: Anguera, Oct. 24: “Forward without fear!”
stories.body: Message No. 5,994, attributed to Our Lady through Pedro Regis in Anguera, Brazil, was given Saturday, Oct. 24, on the eve of the runoff. It asks a return to Jesus and says “tomorrow will be better for men and women of prayer.” It names Confession, the Eucharist, Scripture, the Rosary, consecration to the Immaculate Heart and fidelity to the true Magisterium as “the weapons for your great victory,” and warns of “long years of hard trials,” ending: “Forward without fear!” The local bishop has not issued a judgment on these messages, so they call for prudent discernment.

stories.headline: Wars and rumours of wars: a weekend of missiles and martyrs
stories.body: The weekend gave the Medjugorje message context. Houthi missiles were fired at Saudi cities, mourners were attacked at an Orthodox church in Jordan, 140 drones flew over Ukraine, and today is one year since El Fasher fell. Against that, more than 53 nations’ religious leaders are praying in Assisi through Tuesday. Christ’s words in Matthew 24 apply: “See that you are not alarmed.”

stories.headline: Revival: thousands baptized at Oceanside; UK beach baptisms grow
stories.body: Movement San Diego and Baptize the World held oceanfront mass baptisms in Oceanside, California, on Oct. 17, with thousands taking part, CBN reports. In England, more than 550 people were baptized at Bridlington South Beach on Oct. 10, following earlier beach baptisms at Bigbury. In southeastern Kentucky, five churches joined for a week of revival meetings.
stories.why: Catholic readers will note these are largely evangelical events; the common thread is young adults asking for baptism in unusual numbers.

stories.headline: Eucharistic: new testimony on Guatemala’s Cuilapa Host
stories.body: Three months on, witnesses in Cuilapa, Guatemala, describe a consecrated Host that stayed intact in water for eight days and developed reddish stains. A multidisciplinary team is studying it, and the diocese stresses that only the Holy See can authorize public veneration.

stories.headline: Digital ID and money, soberly: Europe’s next steps
stories.body: The digital euro does not exist yet. The ECB plans a pilot in late 2027 and possible issuance in 2029. Negotiators meet Nov. 5 on holding limits, offline payments, money-laundering rules and fees. Separately, the European Payments Council launched SCARLET to standardize how the coming EU Digital Identity Wallet approves payments. These are real steps toward digital money and identity, and the safeguards in them are being argued in public.
stories.why: What to watch: whether the Nov. 5 deal keeps cash protected and caps how much any person can hold.

beats.title: Miami
beats.headline: Halloween week; VOUS at Bayfront Thursday; Crowder ahead.

stories.headline: Today: Mini Monster Monday at the Children’s Museum
stories.body: Miami Children’s Museum on Watson Island holds Mini Monster Monday today. There’s trick-or-treating at noon and 3:30, a “Creepy Pair of Underwear” show and a little haunted house, and the museum is open 10 to 6. The 3:30 round fits after pickup.

stories.headline: This week: trunk-or-treats and Halloween parties
stories.body: Wednesday at 6 p.m. Miami-Dade Schools Police hosts a trunk-or-treat at 3300 NW 27th Ave. Thursday from 4 to 8, Hialeah Cares throws a Halloween party at Miami Dade College Hialeah. Saturday from 2 to 5:30 there’s a costume party at North Dade Regional Library, plus MiChi-Boo at the Children’s Museum. Tidal Cove’s “Tidal-ween” runs Saturday and Sunday.

stories.headline: Thursday: VOUS Worship “Man Alive,” free at Bayfront Park
stories.body: VOUS Worship brings its “Man Alive” night to the FPL Solar Amphitheater at Bayfront Park on Thursday, Oct. 29. Doors open at 6, the music runs 7 to 10, and admission is free.

stories.headline: Coming up: Crowder, Braveheart Summit and Gilberto Daza
stories.body: Crowder and Rend Collective play Fort Lauderdale on Monday, Nov. 2. The Braveheart men’s summit is Nov. 5 to 7 at One Name Church Miami. Gilberto Daza’s “Buenas Noticias” tour reaches Hialeah on Nov. 14.

beats.title: Pick-me-up
beats.headline: Heat host Dallas at 7:30; a Mandalorian art book.

stories.headline: Tonight at 7:30: Heat look for a first win against Dallas
stories.body: Miami lost 115–110 at Charlotte on Saturday to fall to 0–3. Brandon Miller scored 34 for the Hornets, and Giannis Antetokounmpo was held to 14 in 25 minutes before fouling out with 1:57 left. There is a bright spot: Davion Mitchell is averaging 17 points and shooting 46.7 percent from three. Tonight at 7:30 the Heat host the Mavericks at Kaseya Center. Young star Cooper Flagg is out with a shoulder injury, and Kyrie Irving is expected back. Erik Spoelstra says hard starts are when a team will “collectively build a resolve.”

stories.headline: Star Wars: an art book for The Mandalorian and Grogu
stories.body: The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu, a 256-page hardcover of concept art, sketches and cast interviews, arrives Nov. 3. Elsewhere, Phil Lord and Chris Miller, who left the Han Solo film in 2017, said they would “never say never” to a return.

stories.headline: Star Wars: “Chains can be broken” in Maul’s new teaser
stories.body: StarWars.com has released the teaser for the animated series “Star Wars: Maul – Shadow Lord,” with the tagline “Chains can be broken. Empires can be shattered.” Fans are also marking ten years of Rogue One this season.

stories.headline: Tonight: Darth Vader starts interviewing NFL players
stories.body: Starting tonight on Monday Night Football, an animated Darth Vader interviews real players. The run builds to an all-animated Star Wars telecast of the Super Bowl on Feb. 14, 2027.
